definition: A simple budgeting guide: about 50% of income for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for savings and debt repayment. It is a starting point, not a strict law.

aka: Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions
definition: An international body that issues Shariah and accounting standards for Islamic finance. Pakistan's regulators have adopted many of its standards.
The total percentage gain or loss over a period, without converting it to a yearly figure.
example: NAV goes from PKR 100 to PKR 120 over two years: absolute return is 20%.

definition: A report from the AMC listing your transactions and the units and value you hold.
Coupon earned since the last payment but not yet paid. A buyer of a bond between coupon dates usually pays this to the seller on top of the price.
When one company or investor buys control of another company.
Trying to beat the market by picking specific investments or timing purchases. It usually costs more and many active approaches fail to beat their benchmarks after fees.
The FBR's list of people who have filed their income tax returns. Being on it usually means lower tax deductions on profit, dividends and some transactions.
Income tax paid before the year ends, either in instalments on expected income or deducted on certain transactions. It is adjusted against your final tax when you file.
Your return after taxes like withholding tax or capital gains tax are taken out. It is the return you actually keep and the right one to compare options.
example: A 15% return taxed at 20% leaves a 12% after-tax return.

definition: An income fund allowed to take more risk, such as holding lower-rated or longer-term debt, in search of higher returns. Its NAV can swing more than a normal income fund.
Land used for farming. It can earn income from crops or leasing, and is taxed under provincial rules.
A PSX index covering nearly all listed companies, not just the largest ones. It gives the widest picture of the whole market.
The part of a unit-linked premium kept by the insurer for costs before the rest is invested. It is often high in the first years.
example: With 40% allocation in year one, only PKR 40,000 of a PKR 100,000 premium may be invested.

definition: A preset way of splitting VPS contributions between sub-funds, such as high, medium or low volatility, or a lifecycle plan. Higher equity means higher potential growth and higher risk.
example: A high volatility scheme might put most money in the equity sub-fund; a low volatility scheme mostly in debt and money market.

definition: The process of giving shares to applicants in an IPO or right issue. Those not allotted shares get their money back.
A letter from a housing authority or developer confirming that a specific plot or unit has been assigned to you.
The return an investment earned above what its benchmark and level of risk would predict. Positive alpha suggests skill or an edge; it is hard to achieve consistently.

Investments outside ordinary shares, bonds and cash, such as property, gold, commodities, private businesses, collectibles and crypto. They can add diversification but are often harder to value and sell.
Like depreciation, but for intangible assets such as software or licences.
The average of forecasts made by several analysts, such as expected EPS. Results above or below consensus often move the share price.
Fixing on one number, like the price you paid or a past high, and judging everything against it even when it no longer matters.
example: Refusing to sell a share at Rs 60 because you once saw it at Rs 100.

definition: The yearly meeting where shareholders approve accounts, final dividends, auditor appointments and director elections. Pakistani companies must hold it within a legal time after year-end.
A yearly document with the audited financial statements, directors' report and other company information. Listed companies must send or publish it for shareholders.
Scaling a part-year figure up to a full year. It is a rough estimate because business can be seasonal.
example: Half-year EPS of PKR 4 annualised is about PKR 8.

definition: The steady yearly return that would turn the starting value into the ending value over the period. It makes funds held for different lengths of time comparable.
example: PKR 100 growing to PKR 121 in two years is about 10% a year annualized.

definition: A product bought with a lump sum that pays you a regular income, often for life. It can be used to turn retirement savings into monthly income.
Laws and controls designed to stop criminals from making illegal money look legal. Often paired with CFT, which means countering the financing of terrorism.
Profiting from a price difference for the same thing in two markets by buying cheap and selling dear at the same time. It is low-risk in theory but needs fast execution.
A simple low-requirement bank account aimed at people new to banking, with easier documentation and lower transaction limits.
The lowest price a seller is currently willing to accept for a share. If you buy at market, you usually pay the ask price.
Something you own that has value, such as cash, shares, gold, property or a business.
How your money is divided between types of assets such as shares, debt, cash, gold and property. It is the biggest driver of both risk and return in a portfolio.
example: An investor holds 60% in equity funds, 30% in income funds and 10% in a money market fund.

definition: A fund that can freely shift money between shares, debt and cash based on the manager's market view. It has wider limits than a balanced fund.
A group of investments that behave in similar ways, such as shares (equity), fixed-income, cash, property, gold and commodities.
A company licensed by SECP to create and run mutual funds and pension funds. It picks the investments, handles investor accounts and earns a management fee in return.
example: An AMC may run a money market fund, an equity fund and a VPS pension fund side by side.

definition: Sales divided by total assets. It shows how efficiently a company uses its assets to generate sales.
Things a company owns or controls that have value, such as cash, buildings, machines, stock of goods and money owed by customers.
The total market value of money a fund or AMC manages for investors. It shows size, not performance.
A fee charged to get onto the Active Taxpayers List when a return is filed after the due date. The amount and rules change, so check FBR's latest notice.

The process where SBP, on behalf of the government, sells T-bills, PIBs and Ijara Sukuk to bidders, following a published auction calendar. The results show the yields at which the government borrows.
A statement by independent accountants saying whether the financial statements give a true and fair view. A clean report is a basic quality check.
The maximum amount of share capital a company is allowed to issue under its founding documents. It can be raised with shareholder approval.
Judging how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind, such as overestimating crash risk right after scary news.
An indicator showing how much a share typically moves in a day. Traders use it to set stop-loss distances.
A fee charged when you redeem units, often only if you sell before a set holding period. It is meant to discourage early withdrawals.
example: A fund may charge 1% if you redeem within the first year and nothing after that.

definition: A sale where goods are delivered now and the payment is made later, in one go or instalments, at an agreed price.

The full record of all money flowing between a country and the rest of the world, including the current account and the financial account. A balance of payments crisis happens when a country runs short of foreign currency to pay its bills.
Exports minus imports of goods. A positive number is a trade surplus and a negative number is a trade deficit.
A snapshot of what a company owns (assets), owes (liabilities) and the owners' share (equity) on a given date. Assets always equal liabilities plus equity.
A fund that keeps a mix of shares and debt within set limits, aiming for a balance of growth and stability. It is usually less volatile than an equity fund.
example: A balanced fund might keep roughly half in shares and half in bonds and deposits.

definition: A lottery-style draw used by housing schemes to assign specific plot numbers to file holders.
Selling insurance or takaful policies through a bank's branches and staff. Customers should check that the product suits them and is not confused with a bank deposit.
A free, independent office that handles complaints against banks when the bank itself does not resolve them fairly. You normally must complain to the bank first.
A PSX index of selected liquid commercial bank shares, designed so funds and ETFs can track the banking sector.
A long period when share prices are generally falling and investors are worried. A common rule of thumb is a fall of 20% or more from a recent peak.
A bond or certificate that belongs to whoever holds it, with no owner name recorded. If lost or stolen, the money is effectively gone.
National Savings certificates with monthly profit, available only to senior citizens, widows and persons with disabilities, usually at a higher rate than other schemes.
Holding property or assets in another person's name to hide the real owner. Pakistan has a law prohibiting benami transactions, and such assets can be confiscated.
An index used to judge how well a portfolio or fund has performed. Pakistani equity funds often compare themselves to the KSE-100 or KMI-30.
The real person who ultimately owns or controls an account, asset or company, even if it is held in someone else's name. Regulators require firms to identify beneficial owners.
The person who receives the insurance payout if the insured person dies.
A measure of how much a share tends to move compared to the overall market. A beta above 1 means it usually swings more than the index; below 1 means it swings less.
example: A share with a beta of 1.5 might rise about 15% when the KSE-100 rises 10%.

definition: The highest price a buyer is currently willing to pay for a share. If you sell at market, you usually get the bid price.
The gap between the best bid and the best ask. A small spread means a share is easy to trade; a wide spread means trading it costs more.
example: Bid PKR 99.50 and ask PKR 100.00 means a spread of 50 paisa.

definition: The gap between the price at which an insurer sells units in its funds and the price at which it buys them back. It is a hidden cost in unit-linked plans.
Confirming your identity by matching your fingerprints or face with NADRA's records. It is used for opening accounts, SIM cards and some withdrawals.
The first and largest cryptocurrency, with a fixed maximum supply. Its price can rise or fall very sharply in short periods.
A rare, unexpected event with a huge impact, like a pandemic or sudden war. Such events are why diversification and emergency funds matter.
A single very large trade of shares, usually between institutions, arranged privately at an agreed price. In Pakistan these often go through the negotiated deal market.
A shared digital record of transactions copied across many computers, which makes it very hard to change past entries. Cryptocurrencies run on blockchains.
A share of a large, well-known and financially strong company with a long record of profits and often dividends. Considered safer, though never risk-free.
A meeting of the company's directors to approve results, declare dividends and make big decisions. Listed companies in Pakistan must tell PSX in advance and announce outcomes promptly.
The group elected by shareholders to oversee the company and its management. Pakistani listed companies must include independent directors under corporate governance rules.
Two lines drawn above and below a moving average, set by how volatile the price has been. Prices near the upper band are relatively high; near the lower band, relatively low.
A loan you give to a government or company in exchange for regular payments and the return of your money at the end. The bond can often be sold to someone else before it ends.
Free extra shares given to existing shareholders in proportion to what they own, instead of cash. The share price usually adjusts down so total value stays about the same.
example: A 20% bonus means you get 20 new shares for every 100 you hold.

definition: Extra fund units given to you instead of cash when a fund distributes profit.

A way of setting an IPO price where large investors bid the price and quantity they want, and the final strike price is set from that demand. In Pakistan, part of the issue is then offered to the general public at that price.
A period announced by a company when it closes its share register to decide who gets a dividend, bonus, right shares or a vote. Shareholders on record before it begins receive the entitlement.
The value of a company according to its balance sheet: total assets minus total liabilities. It is an accounting figure and can differ a lot from market value.
Shareholders' equity divided by the number of shares. In Pakistan it is often called the breakup value per share.
example: Equity of PKR 500 crore and 10 crore shares give a breakup value of PKR 50 per share.

definition: Banking through a mobile app or agent shop without visiting a bank branch, such as sending money, paying bills and saving small amounts.
When a price falls below a support level. It is often seen as a sign that further falls may follow.
When a price moves above a resistance level or out of a trading range, often with high volume. Traders see it as a sign that a new move up may begin.
The fee a broker charges for each buy or sell order, usually a percentage of the trade value or a fixed amount per share. Taxes and exchange fees are added on top.
example: On a made-up PKR 100,000 trade with 0.15% commission, you pay PKR 150 plus taxes.

definition: When prices rise far above what the underlying business is really worth, driven by hype and the hope of selling to someone else at a higher price. Bubbles usually end in sharp falls.
A long period when share prices are generally rising and investors feel confident. Being bullish means expecting prices to go up.
The repeating pattern of an economy growing, peaking, slowing and recovering. Different investments tend to do better at different stages.
Buying good shares and keeping them for many years, ignoring short-term ups and downs. It relies on business growth and dividends over time.
A way to buy something now and pay in instalments, often presented as interest-free. Missed payments can bring fees, and many small plans can add up to more debt than you realise.
The steady yearly growth rate that would take a value from its starting level to its ending level over several years.
example: Sales growing from PKR 100 crore to PKR 200 crore over 5 years is a CAGR of about 15%.

definition: A bond the issuer can repay early, usually when rates fall, which can cut the investor's expected returns.
A chart bar showing a period's open, high, low and close. The thick body shows open to close; thin lines called wicks show the high and low. Green or hollow usually means the price closed higher.
The increase in an asset's price over time. Property and shares can deliver returns through appreciation as well as income.
Money spent on buying or upgrading long-term physical assets like plants and machinery.

Tax on the profit you make when you sell an asset, like shares, mutual fund units or property, for more than you paid. For listed shares in Pakistan it is generally calculated and collected through NCCPL; rates depend on the asset, holding period, purchase date and filer status and change often, so check the latest rules.
example: Buy shares for Rs 100,000 and sell for Rs 130,000: the Rs 30,000 profit is the capital gain that may be taxed.

definition: The loss when you sell an asset for less than you paid. Tax rules may allow some capital losses to be set off against capital gains; check current FBR rules.
An investment goal focused on protecting the original amount rather than growing it fast. It suits short-term goals and emergency money.

A fund that aims to return at least your original investment if you stay until a set maturity date, while trying to earn extra from a small share investment. Protection usually applies only if you hold to maturity.
example: Of PKR 100,000, most goes into deposits that grow back to PKR 100,000 by maturity; the rest goes into shares for upside.

definition: A tax charged on the value of certain assets, such as buying some immovable property or holding certain assets. Who pays it and at what rate depends on federal and provincial law, which changes.
Money spent on assets that are still being built, such as a new plant. It moves into fixed assets when the project is complete.
Financing from a bank to buy a vehicle, repaid in monthly instalments, usually with a down payment and the car as security. Cars lose value over time, so this debt does not build wealth.
Cash in hand and at banks, plus very short-term investments that can be turned into cash almost immediately.
Inventory days plus receivable days minus payable days. It shows how long cash is tied up in the business before it comes back. Shorter is generally better.
Very safe, very liquid holdings that can be turned into cash almost immediately, like bank savings and money market funds.
The money coming in and going out over a period. Positive cash flow means you have money left over to save or invest.

A report showing how cash came into and went out of a company over a period, split into operating, investing and financing activities. Profit and cash are not the same, and this statement shows the difference.
A futures contract where no shares change hands at expiry; only the price difference is paid in cash. PSX offers these on selected stocks.
CDC keeps shares in electronic form, like a bank keeps money. When you buy shares on PSX, they are recorded in your account in CDC's system instead of on paper certificates.
A CDC account opened in your name through your broker. Your shares are held in it, but the broker operates it on your behalf, so you should check your CDC statements regularly.
The government body under the Finance Ministry that runs National Savings schemes and prize bonds. Its rates are revised from time to time.
The company that holds shares and other securities electronically on behalf of investors, so no paper certificates are needed. It also acts as trustee for many mutual funds.
The electronic record-keeping system run by CDC that holds and transfers shares between accounts. It replaced physical share certificates for most trading in Pakistan.
Money set aside by an Islamic fund or bank for charity, such as from purification or late payment penalties, which cannot be counted as its own income.
The process of moving money from the payer's bank to the receiver's bank after a cheque is deposited. Funds are not usable until clearing is done.

A rule that limits how far a share or index can move in one day, or pauses trading after a very large move. It gives investors time to calm down during panic or mania. PSX applies limits to individual shares and to the market index.
example: If a share's daily limit were 7.5% and LDCP were PKR 100, it could not trade above PKR 107.50 that day.

definition: A chain of unpaid bills in Pakistan's energy sector, where distribution companies, power producers, fuel suppliers and the government owe each other money. It grows from losses, theft, unpaid bills and prices set below cost, and weighs on energy company cash flows.
A formal request to the insurer to pay out under the policy after an insured event.
A bond's quoted price without accrued interest.
The behind-the-scenes process of matching and confirming trades and working out who owes what to whom. In Pakistan NCCPL does this for PSX trades.
A period, usually around the release of financial results, when directors and other insiders are not allowed to trade the company's shares.
A fund that raises a fixed amount once and then trades on the stock exchange like a share. Its market price can be above or below its NAV because it depends on buyers and sellers.
example: A closed-end fund with NAV PKR 15 might trade on PSX at PKR 12, a discount of 20%.

definition: The official final price of a share at the end of a trading day. It is used to value portfolios and calculate the next day's price limits.
The national identity card issued by NADRA, needed for almost every bank, investment and savings account in Pakistan.
An asset you pledge to a lender that they can take if you fail to repay, such as a house, car, gold or shares.
Short-term unsecured debt issued by strong companies to borrow for less than a year.
Property used for business, such as shops, offices and warehouses. It often earns higher rent than residential property but can stay empty longer.

An informal savings group where members pay a fixed amount every month and one member takes the whole pot each round. It earns no profit and depends on trust, so a member who stops paying can cause losses.
example: 10 friends each pay Rs 10,000 a month; each month one of them receives Rs 100,000 until all have had a turn.

definition: A basic raw material that is traded in bulk and is the same wherever it comes from, such as oil, gold, wheat, cotton or coal. Commodity prices affect inflation and many company profits.
A fund that invests in commodities such as gold, usually through exchange contracts, so investors can gain from price changes without storing the metal.
An auction bid stating both the amount and the yield or price the bidder wants. It is accepted only if it falls within the cut-off.
Earning returns on both your original money and the returns already earned. Over long periods it makes savings grow much faster. Formula: future value = amount x (1 + rate) ^ years.
example: Rs 100,000 at 10% a year compounds to about Rs 259,000 in 10 years.

definition: Earning profit on your past profit as well as on your original money. The more often profit is added, the faster money grows.
example: PKR 100,000 at 10% a year becomes PKR 110,000 after one year and PKR 121,000 after two.

definition: The danger of having too much of your money in one investment, company, sector or asset. If that one thing goes wrong, your losses are large.
The set of policy conditions a lender, such as the IMF, attaches to a loan. They are meant to fix the problems that caused the funding need.
Paying attention only to information that supports what you already believe and ignoring evidence against it.
Accounts that combine the parent company and its subsidiaries as if they were one business. They give the fuller picture of a group.

An index that tracks the prices of a fixed basket of goods and services that households typically buy. In Pakistan it is published monthly by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, with separate urban and rural measures, and its yearly change is the headline inflation figure.
When trouble in one market, company or country spreads to others, causing wider falls.
Possible obligations that depend on a future event, such as a pending court case or tax dispute. They appear in the notes and can be important risks.
The month in which a futures contract expires. PSX futures are listed for upcoming months so traders can choose how far ahead to trade.
Moving money from one fund to another within the same AMC without first taking it out to your bank.
example: Switching PKR 300,000 from an equity fund to a money market fund after a strong market rally.

definition: A finer measure showing that the price-yield link is curved, so duration alone slightly misjudges price changes when rates move a lot.
Inflation measured after removing items whose prices jump around a lot, mainly food and energy. It shows the underlying, more persistent trend in prices and is watched closely by the central bank.
Any event started by a company that affects its shares or shareholders, such as dividends, bonus shares, right issues, splits, mergers or buybacks.
Sukuk issued by a company rather than the government, often with returns linked to KIBOR and a credit rating like TFCs.
A fall in prices, often around 10%, after a strong rise. It is usually seen as a pause rather than the start of a long decline.
How closely two investments move together, from +1 (always together) to -1 (always opposite). Combining assets with low correlation improves diversification.
The return shareholders expect for taking the risk of owning a company's shares. In Pakistan it is often built from the government bond yield plus an extra return for equity risk.
The direct cost of making or buying the goods a company sold, such as raw materials, factory labour and factory power.
The risk that the other side of a deal, such as a broker, bank, developer or borrower, fails to deliver what it promised.
The regular profit payment a bond pays to its holder.
example: A PKR 100,000 bond with a 12% coupon paid twice a year pays PKR 6,000 every six months.

definition: The yearly coupon shown as a percentage of the bond's face value.

The yearly cost of borrowing on a credit card, including interest or markup and some fees. Card rates are usually far higher than most investments can reliably earn, so carrying a balance is expensive.
The maximum amount a bank allows you to borrow on a credit card or credit line.
A grade from a rating agency showing how likely a borrower is to repay on time. AAA is the strongest; lower grades mean more risk and usually a higher yield.
A company licensed by SECP to rate borrowers, debt and funds. In Pakistan the main local agencies are PACRA and VIS.
A record of your loans, cards and repayment behaviour kept by credit bureaus, including SBP's eCIB. Late payments can make it harder to get loans later.
The risk that a borrower will not repay what it owes. Higher credit risk usually means a higher promised return to compensate.
The extra yield a corporate bond pays over a similar government security to make up for its higher risk.
example: A TFC yielding 15% when a similar PIB yields 12% has a 3% credit spread.

definition: A platform for buying and selling cryptocurrencies. Using an unregulated exchange means your money may not be protected if it is hacked or shuts down.
Software or a device that stores the keys needed to access your crypto. Whoever has the keys controls the coins.
Trading with the entitlement still attached. Buying a share cum-dividend, before the ex-date, means you will receive the coming dividend.
A rise in a currency's value against another. When the rupee appreciates, imports get cheaper in rupees.
A fall in a currency's value due to market forces. When the rupee depreciates, you need more rupees to buy one dollar.
The risk that changes in exchange rates reduce the value of an investment or increase a cost. For Pakistanis, a weaker rupee raises the cost of foreign education, travel and imports.
A report that regulated firms send to authorities when cash transactions cross a set threshold, regardless of whether they look suspicious.
A bank account for daily use with unlimited deposits and withdrawals, cheques and cards, that pays no profit. In Islamic banks it is usually based on Qard (a loan to the bank).
When a country spends more foreign currency on imports, services and income payments than it earns. It must be funded by loans, investment or reserves, and large deficits often pressure the rupee.
Assets expected to be turned into cash or used up within a year, such as cash, inventory and receivables.
Debts and obligations due within a year, such as supplier bills, short-term loans and the current part of long-term loans.
Current assets divided by current liabilities. A ratio above 1 means the company has more short-term assets than short-term debts.
A bond's yearly coupon divided by its current market price. It ignores any gain or loss at maturity.
example: A PKR 12 coupon on a bond priced at PKR 96 gives a current yield of 12.5%.

definition: The deeper process of understanding a customer, their source of funds and the purpose of their account, and keeping that information up to date. Higher-risk customers get enhanced due diligence.
A tax on goods imported into the country. Changes in customs and regulatory duties can affect prices and the profits of local manufacturers.
The time by which a fund must receive your buy or sell request to process it at that day's price. Requests after the cut-off get the next dealing day's price.
The highest yield the government accepts in an auction. Bids at or below this yield are accepted, and it is a key signal of where market rates are heading.
A share whose profits rise and fall strongly with the economy, such as cement, steel or autos. They tend to do well in booms and badly in slowdowns.

A sworn declaration form used in Pakistan to claim exemption from compulsory Zakat deduction on bank accounts and certain investments, for example on grounds of faith or school of thought. It is submitted to the bank or fund manager before the deduction date.
An order that is valid only for the trading day it is placed. If it is not filled by the close, it is cancelled automatically.
Buying and selling the same share within one trading day to profit from small moves. It is risky and costs add up because of frequent commissions.
A day on which a fund accepts purchase and redemption requests, normally a bank working day.
The amount paid to the beneficiary if the insured person dies while the policy is active.
When a short-term moving average crosses below a long-term one. Many traders read it as a bearish signal.
Paying off debts starting with the one that has the highest rate, while making minimum payments on the rest. It saves the most money.
Replacing a loan that is due with a new loan instead of paying it off. Countries often ask friendly lenders to roll over deposits or loans to avoid a cash crunch.
Paying the interest and principal due on loans. When a large share of government revenue goes to debt servicing, less is left for development.
Paying off the smallest debt first for a quick win, then moving to the next smallest. It costs more than the avalanche but can keep you motivated.
Total debt divided by shareholders' equity. A high ratio means the company relies heavily on borrowed money, which raises risk.
example: Debt of PKR 60 crore and equity of PKR 100 crore give a D/E of 0.6.

definition: Public debt divided by GDP. A higher ratio means the debt is larger compared with the economy's ability to repay.
Your monthly debt payments divided by your monthly income. A high ratio means a big share of income goes to debt and leaves little to save.
example: Rs 40,000 of instalments on a Rs 160,000 income is a 25% ratio.

definition: An equity fund made mainly for other funds, such as fund of funds or pension schemes, to invest in rather than for direct retail buying.
The part of a loss you must pay yourself before the insurer pays the rest.
example: With a PKR 10,000 deductible, a PKR 50,000 car repair claim pays PKR 40,000.

definition: Income the law assumes you earned even if you did not receive cash, such as notional income on certain property. Rules on deemed income change, so check the current law.
When a borrower misses a required payment on its debt.
The chance a borrower fails to pay coupons or principal on time.
A separate PSX segment where shares of companies that have broken listing rules, such as not holding meetings or not publishing accounts, are moved. Being placed there is a strong warning sign.
Long-term National Savings certificates where profit builds up and is paid with the principal at maturity, giving compounding. Early encashment earns less.
example: An investor buys PKR 100,000 of DSCs to fund a child's education years later.

definition: A share of a company whose products people buy in good and bad times, such as food, medicine or power. Its profits are usually steadier than the economy.
Tax that will be paid or saved in the future because accounting profit and taxable profit are counted differently over time.
A general fall in prices over time, the opposite of inflation. It sounds good but can signal weak demand and a slowing economy.
When a company's shares are removed from the exchange, so they can no longer be traded there. It can be forced for rule breaches or done voluntarily.
A PSX futures contract on a single stock where, at expiry, the actual shares are delivered and paid for. If you hold it to expiry, you must take or give delivery.
A bank-issued payment instrument used to send guaranteed money, traditionally to another city.
Splitting part of a company's business into a separate company, with existing shareholders receiving shares in the new company.
A safety scheme that repays depositors up to a set limit if a member bank fails. In Pakistan it is run by the Deposit Protection Corporation.
A subsidiary of SBP that runs the deposit protection scheme. Banks pay premiums to it, and it compensates eligible depositors up to a limit per depositor per bank if a bank fails.
Spreading the cost of a physical asset, like a machine, over the years it is used. It reduces profit each year but is not a cash payment.
A financial contract whose value comes from something else, such as a share, an index or a commodity. Futures and options are common derivatives.
A deliberate or allowed sharp fall in a currency's value against other currencies. It makes imports and foreign debt more expensive in rupees but can help exports.
A government body that plans a city and approves housing schemes and building plans, such as the Capital Development Authority in Islamabad. Its website often lists approved and illegal schemes.
A REIT that raises money to build new property projects and earns from selling or renting them once complete. It carries more risk because projects can face delays or cost overruns.
EPS calculated as if all convertible securities and options had been turned into shares. It is the more cautious version of EPS.
When a company issues new shares, each existing share owns a smaller slice of the company and its profits.
A partnership used for home and car finance where the bank and customer jointly own an asset; the customer pays rent for the bank's share and slowly buys that share until owning it fully.
example: A bank owns 80% of a house; each month the customer pays rent plus buys a bit more of the bank's share.

definition: A tax paid directly by the person or company it is charged on, such as income tax.
A bond's price including accrued interest; this is what the buyer actually pays.
When a bond's market price is lower than its face value, usually because its coupon is lower than current market rates or because it pays no coupon.
example: A PKR 100 bond trading at PKR 96 is at a PKR 4 discount.

definition: The yearly return used to convert future cash into today's value in a DCF. Higher risk or higher interest rates mean a higher discount rate and a lower value.

A valuation method that estimates future cash flows and converts them into today's value, because money received later is worth less than money today. The result is very sensitive to the assumptions used.
When inflation is still positive but slowing down. Prices are still rising, just more slowly than before.
example: Inflation falling from 20% to 12% is disinflation; prices still went up 12%.

definition: The habit of selling winning investments too early to lock in gains while holding losers too long hoping they recover.
Spreading your money across different companies, sectors and asset types so one bad investment does not hurt you too much.
A part of a company's profit paid to shareholders, usually in cash. In Pakistan dividends are often announced as a percentage of face value or as rupees per share.
example: A 25% dividend on a PKR 10 face value share means PKR 2.50 per share.

definition: EPS divided by dividend per share. It shows how many times the dividend could be paid from profits; a low cover means the dividend may be at risk.
A valuation method that values a share as the present value of its expected future dividends. It suits steady dividend payers.
example: With a PKR 10 dividend next year, 15% required return and 5% growth: value = 10 / (0.15 - 0.05) = PKR 100.

definition: Profit paid out by a fund to unit holders, either in cash or as extra units. After a payout the NAV drops by about the same amount, so your total wealth does not change on that day.
The share of net profit paid out as dividends. It equals dividend per share divided by EPS.
example: EPS of PKR 10 and DPS of PKR 6 give a 60% payout ratio.

definition: The total cash dividend paid for a period divided by the number of shares, shown in rupees per share.
A share of a company that regularly pays a good portion of its profits as cash dividends. Popular with investors who want steady income.
The payment of a cash dividend. In Pakistan listed companies pay dividends electronically into the shareholder's registered bank account, so your IBAN must be on record.
Yearly dividend per share divided by the share price, as a percentage. It shows the cash return from dividends at today's price.
example: A PKR 8 yearly dividend on a PKR 100 share is an 8% dividend yield.

definition: A candlestick where the open and close are almost the same, giving a very thin body. It signals indecision between buyers and sellers.
When people switch their savings or prices into US dollars because they lose trust in the local currency. It often rises during high inflation or currency crises.
A bank account with no customer activity for a long time, which the bank blocks for safety until the customer reactivates it with fresh identification.
A double top is two peaks at about the same level, suggesting the rise is running out of steam. A double bottom is the opposite, two lows suggesting a fall may be ending.
The part of a purchase price you pay upfront in cash, with the rest financed by a loan.
example: On a Rs 5,000,000 car, a 30% down payment is Rs 1,500,000.

definition: The fall in value from a previous peak to a later low, usually as a percentage. It shows how much you could have been down at the worst point.
example: A portfolio that falls from Rs 1,000,000 to Rs 750,000 has a 25% drawdown.

definition: Researching and checking an investment carefully before putting money in, such as verifying licences, documents, track record and risks.
Breaking ROE into three parts: net margin, asset turnover and leverage. It shows whether high ROE comes from strong profits, efficient use of assets, or heavy borrowing.
A measure, in years, of how long on average it takes to get a bond's cash back. It also shows how sensitive the price is to interest rate changes: higher duration means bigger price swings.
Voting on shareholder resolutions online or by mail instead of attending in person. Pakistani law allows these options for certain resolutions.
How fast a company's profits rise from one period to the next, usually shown as a percentage.
Net profit divided by the number of shares outstanding. It shows how much profit each share earned.
example: Net profit of PKR 50 crore and 10 crore shares give EPS of PKR 5.

definition: How real and repeatable a company's profits are. High-quality earnings come from the core business and are backed by cash, not one-off gains or accounting choices.
When reported profit is noticeably higher (a beat) or lower (a miss) than what analysts expected.
EPS divided by share price, the reverse of P/E, shown as a percentage. It is handy for comparing shares with returns on savings or bonds.
example: A P/E of 5 means an earnings yield of 20%.

aka: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation
definition: Operating profit with depreciation and amortisation added back. It gives a rough view of cash earnings from operations, but ignores the cost of replacing assets and paying debt.
EBITDA as a percentage of sales. It is used to compare operating profitability across companies with different debt and asset levels.
A lasting advantage that protects a company's profits from competitors, such as a strong brand, low costs, licences or network effects.
Total tax paid divided by total income. It shows the true share of your income going to tax.
example: Paying Rs 150,000 tax on Rs 1,500,000 income is a 10% effective rate.

definition: Money set aside in a safe, easily accessible place to cover unexpected costs like job loss or medical bills. A common guide is several months of essential expenses.
example: If your essential costs are Rs 80,000 a month, a 6-month emergency fund would be Rs 480,000.

definition: Turning a certificate, bond or units into cash, either at maturity or earlier.
A policy that combines life cover with savings. It pays on death during the term or a maturity amount if you survive it, but returns are often modest after costs.
A two-candle pattern where the second candle's body fully covers the first one's body in the opposite direction. It can hint that the trend is reversing.
Market cap plus debt minus cash. It estimates what it would cost to buy the whole business, including taking over its debts.
What a shareholder is due from a corporate action, such as cash dividend, bonus shares or the right to buy new shares.
A Pakistani government institution that provides old-age pensions and some other benefits to registered private-sector workers, funded by employer and employee contributions.
In investing, equity means owning shares rather than lending money. In accounting it also means what the owners' stake in a company is worth on its books.
A fund that invests mostly in shares of listed companies. It can grow more over long periods but its NAV can fall sharply when the stock market drops.
The extra return investors demand for owning shares instead of risk-free government securities.
Enterprise value divided by EBITDA. It compares companies' values regardless of how much debt they carry.
The first trading day on which buying the share no longer gives you the upcoming dividend, bonus or right. The price usually drops by about the value of the entitlement on this day.
example: If a PKR 5 dividend goes ex today, a share that closed at PKR 100 may open near PKR 95.

definition: The NAV of a fund right after a payout has been removed from it. It is lower than the NAV before the payout by the payout amount.
example: NAV PKR 110 before a PKR 10 payout becomes an ex-NAV of PKR 100.

definition: The price of one currency in terms of another. In Pakistan it is usually quoted as how many rupees one US dollar costs.
example: If USD 1 = Rs 280, a USD 100 phone import costs Rs 28,000 before taxes.

definition: A fund, usually tracking an index, whose units are bought and sold on the stock exchange through a broker during market hours. It combines the low cost of an index fund with the ease of trading a share.
example: An ETF tracking a basket of 30 large PSX companies can be bought in your brokerage account like any listed share.

definition: A situation listed in the policy that is not covered, such as certain pre-existing illnesses.
The rate an Islamic bank estimates depositors will earn. The final rate is declared after the pool's actual results are known.
The last day a futures or options contract exists. After this, the contract is settled by delivery or cash.
A moving average that gives more weight to recent prices, so it reacts faster to new moves than a simple moving average.
An extra deposit required on top of the basic margin to cover the risk of large price moves. NCCPL sets such margins for PSX trades.
Money a country's government, banks and companies owe to foreign lenders, usually in foreign currency. It becomes harder to repay when the rupee weakens.
A shareholder meeting called outside the AGM to decide urgent or special matters, such as a right issue, merger or change in company name.
The fixed value printed on a share when it is issued, which is often PKR 10 in Pakistan. It is not the market price, but dividends and bonuses in Pakistan are announced as a percentage of it.
Takaful that covers life and often includes savings or investment, similar to life insurance.
An official extract from land revenue records showing who owns a piece of land and how much. It is commonly checked before buying land in Pakistan.

An international body that sets standards against money laundering and terrorist financing. Countries with weaknesses can be placed on a monitoring list, often called the grey list, which can hurt foreign investment and banking ties.
A formal opinion by a qualified Islamic scholar or board stating whether something is permitted.
Pakistan's federal tax authority. It collects income tax, sales tax on goods, customs and federal excise, and publishes the Active Taxpayers List.

The government's yearly plan for revenue, taxes and spending, presented to parliament through a Finance Bill. In Pakistan it is announced before the new fiscal year starts in July and often changes taxes on savings and investments.
A federal tax charged on specific goods and services, such as cigarettes, drinks or some financial services.
The ombudsman that handles complaints against the FBR, such as delayed refunds or unfair treatment.
Charges like brokerage commission, fund fees, taxes and spreads that reduce your return. Small yearly fees add up to a big difference over many years.
Lines drawn at set percentages, such as 38.2%, 50% and 61.8%, of a previous price move. Traders watch them as possible support or resistance levels during pullbacks.
A legal duty to act in someone else's best interest, such as a fund manager or trustee acting for investors rather than for themselves.
A person whose name appears on the FBR's Active Taxpayers List, usually because they filed their income tax return. Filers generally pay lower withholding tax on many transactions than non-filers.
The dividend announced after full-year results. It is recommended by the board and approved by shareholders at the annual general meeting.
A system where tax withheld on certain income, such as some dividends or bank profit, counts as your full and final tax on that income. That income is then not added to your other income for tax.
Interest or markup paid on borrowings. High finance costs can eat up profits, especially when interest rates rise. Pakistani accounts often use the word markup.
The part of the balance of payments that records investment and loan flows, such as foreign direct investment, portfolio investment and borrowing. It often funds a current account deficit.
A specific money target with an amount and date, like saving Rs 2,000,000 for a car in 4 years. Clear goals make it easier to choose the right investments.
Understanding basic money concepts like budgeting, interest, inflation, risk and debt well enough to make good decisions.
Pakistan's financial intelligence unit. Banks, brokers and others send it reports of suspicious or large transactions to help fight money laundering and terrorist financing.
When a listed company publishes its profit or loss for a quarter, half-year or full year. In Pakistan these are announced to PSX, often together with any dividend or bonus.
The formal reports showing a company's performance and financial position: the balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement and statement of changes in equity, plus notes.
Cash raised from or paid to lenders and shareholders, such as new loans, loan repayments, share issues and dividends.
Data showing how much foreign investors bought or sold on PSX in a period. NCCPL publishes it, and big foreign buying or selling often moves the market.
When the government spends more than it collects in revenue in a year. The gap is filled by borrowing, which adds to public debt.
example: If revenue is Rs 10 trillion and spending is Rs 16 trillion, the fiscal deficit is Rs 6 trillion.

definition: The 12-month period a company uses for its accounts. Many Pakistani companies use a July to June year, while others, such as banks, use the calendar year.
Costs that stay about the same each month, like rent, school fees or loan instalments.
Investments that pay regular, mostly predictable income, such as government securities, bank deposits and income funds. They are usually less volatile than shares.
A PIB whose coupon rate stays the same for its whole life. Its market price falls when interest rates rise and rises when rates fall.
A fund or plan that locks money in debt for a set term so the expected return is largely known at the start. Leaving early may cost a back-end load.
A PIB whose coupon resets regularly based on a benchmark, such as a recent T-bill auction yield, plus or minus a spread. Its price moves less with rate changes than a fixed PIB.
The minimum price at which investors can bid during book building. Bids below it are not accepted.
The anxious feeling that everyone else is making money and you will be left behind, which pushes people to buy in a hurry, often near the top.
example: Buying a share only because friends say it doubled last month is FOMO.

definition: A bank account held in a foreign currency such as US dollars, euros or pounds instead of rupees. It protects savings from rupee falls but has its own rules on deposits and withdrawals.
Keeping savings in foreign currency, like US dollars, to protect against rupee weakness. It earns little on its own, and cash held at home carries theft risk.
Long-term investment by foreigners in a country's businesses, such as building factories or buying a large stake in a company. It is considered more stable than short-term flows.

Foreign currency and other liquid assets, like gold, held to pay for imports and repay foreign debt. In Pakistan they are reported as reserves held by the State Bank and those held by commercial banks.
Foreign money invested in a country's shares and debt securities without taking control of companies. It can enter and leave quickly.
Share price divided by expected EPS for the coming year, based on forecasts. It depends on how accurate the estimates are.
The rule that fund units are bought or sold at a price worked out after the cut-off time, not at the last known price. This stops anyone trading on old prices.
Making different choices depending on how the same information is presented, such as '90% success' versus '10% failure'.
Operating cash flow minus capital expenditure. It is the cash left over that can pay dividends, reduce debt or fund growth.
example: Operating cash flow of PKR 80 crore minus capex of PKR 30 crore gives free cash flow of PKR 50 crore.

definition: The shares that are actually available for public trading, excluding those held by sponsors, the government, directors and other strategic holders. A low free float can make prices jumpy.
example: If a company has 100 crore shares and sponsors hold 70 crore, the free float is 30 crore shares (30%).

definition: The market value of only the freely tradable shares. PSX indices like the KSE-100 are weighted using free-float market cap, not total market cap.
A way of building an index where bigger companies count more, but only their freely tradable shares are counted. PSX's main indices use this method.
A short period after you receive a new policy during which you can cancel it and get your premium back, minus small allowed costs.
When a broker or insider trades ahead of a big client order they know about, profiting from the price move it will cause. It is illegal.
A one-time fee charged when you buy units, taken as a percentage of the amount invested. It reduces the money that actually gets invested.
example: Investing PKR 100,000 with a 3% front-end load means only about PKR 97,000 worth of units are bought.

definition: The professional at an AMC who decides what a fund buys and sells, within the fund's rules.
A monthly report from an AMC for each fund showing NAV, returns, top holdings, asset mix, credit quality, fees and risk level. It is the quickest way to check what a fund is doing.
A fund that invests in other mutual funds instead of buying shares or bonds directly. It gives ready-made diversification, but there may be fees at both levels.
example: A fund of funds plan might hold an equity fund and an income fund in a set ratio based on the investor's risk level.

definition: A grade given by a rating agency such as PACRA or VIS. For income and money market funds it shows how stable the fund is (for example a rating ending in '(f)'); for other funds it may rank past performance against peers.
example: An income fund rated AA(f) is judged to have high stability of returns.

definition: Judging a share by studying the company's business, profits, debts, management and industry to estimate what it is really worth.
The difference between a futures price and the ready-market price of the same share. Traders sometimes buy in one market and sell in the other to earn this gap.
An agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date. Both sides must honour it, and only a margin is paid upfront, so gains and losses are magnified.
The part of the exchange where futures contracts are traded instead of the shares themselves. PSX offers deliverable and cash-settled futures on selected stocks and indices.
Believing that a run of results makes the opposite more likely next, like thinking a share must rise because it has fallen five days in a row.
When a share opens well above or below the previous close, leaving an empty space on the chart. Gaps often follow big overnight news.
The percentage change in GDP from one period to the next, after adjusting for inflation. Faster growth usually means more jobs and higher company profits.
How much of a company's funding comes from debt compared to equity, often shown as debt divided by debt plus equity. Highly geared companies suffer more when profits fall or interest rates rise.
A PSX board for listing smaller and growing companies with lighter listing requirements. Shares on it can be riskier and are usually open to qualified investors.
Takaful covering property, vehicles, health, travel and other non-life risks.
Expecting very large returns in a short time with little risk. It makes people easy targets for scams and reckless bets.
Excessive uncertainty or vagueness in a contract, such as unclear price or subject matter, which Islamic finance forbids.
A legal document transferring an asset, like property, to someone as a gift without payment. Gifts may have tax and documentation implications that should be checked.
Investing separately for specific goals, such as a child's education, Hajj, a house or retirement, with a target amount, deadline and risk level for each.
The assumption that a company will keep operating for the foreseeable future. If the auditor raises doubts about it, the company may be in serious financial trouble.

A precious metal that many Pakistanis hold as savings and protection against inflation and rupee weakness. Its local price depends mainly on the global price and the dollar-rupee rate; it pays no income.
When a short-term moving average, often the 50-day, crosses above a long-term one, often the 200-day. Many traders read it as a bullish signal.

Good debt is borrowing at a reasonable cost for something likely to grow your income or wealth, like education or a business. Bad debt is costly borrowing for things that lose value, like gadgets on a credit card.
An order that stays open across several days until it is filled or you cancel it. A day order, by contrast, expires when the trading day ends.
The extra amount paid when buying a company above the fair value of its net assets. It reflects things like brand and customer base, and can be written down if the purchase disappoints.

Shariah compliant government securities based on Ijarah, where investors own a share of government assets and receive rental payments instead of interest. They come in fixed and variable rental types.
Debt issued by the Government of Pakistan, such as T-bills, PIBs and GoP Ijara Sukuk. SBP sells them on the government's behalf through auctions.
Extra time after a premium is due during which you can still pay without losing cover.
A lump-sum payment some employers give when an employee leaves or retires, usually based on years of service and last salary.
The two emotions that drive many market swings: greed pushes people to buy at high prices, and fear pushes them to sell at low prices.
An option letting the issuer sell extra shares beyond the planned amount if demand in an offering is strong.
The total value of all goods and services produced inside a country in a period, usually a year. It is the main measure of the size of an economy.
Gross profit as a percentage of sales. It shows how much of each rupee of sales is left after direct production costs.
example: Gross profit of PKR 25 on sales of PKR 100 is a 25% gross margin.

definition: Revenue minus cost of sales. It shows how much is left from sales to cover other expenses.
example: Sales of PKR 1,000 crore and cost of sales of PKR 750 crore give gross profit of PKR 250 crore.

definition: A share of a company expected to grow its sales and profits faster than average. Such shares often pay small dividends and trade at high valuations.
A unit type that keeps profits inside the fund instead of paying them out, so the NAV keeps rising.
An adult legally responsible for a minor's affairs, including operating accounts or investments opened in the child's name until they come of age.
A reduction applied to the value of shares used as collateral to allow for price falls. A share worth PKR 100 with a 30% haircut counts as only PKR 70 of collateral.
Results covering the first six months of the financial year. In Pakistan these are reviewed by the auditor, though not fully audited.
A candlestick with a small body near the top and a long lower wick, appearing after a fall. It suggests sellers pushed prices down but buyers pushed them back up.
A chart pattern with three peaks, the middle one highest, that often appears at the end of an uptrend. A fall below its base line is read as a bearish signal.
The overall inflation number that includes all items in the price basket, including food and fuel. It is the figure most often reported in the news.
Insurance that pays for hospital and medical costs up to set limits.
An investment or action taken to reduce the risk of loss on another holding, like insurance for your portfolio. Hedging usually costs something or limits gains.
example: Keeping some savings in gold to soften losses if the rupee falls sharply.

definition: Taking a position that offsets possible losses in another investment, like buying insurance. It lowers risk but also limits gains.
Following what most other people are doing instead of thinking independently. It can push prices too high in booms and too low in panics.
A voluntary gift. Islamic banks may give extra amounts to depositors as hiba, but it cannot be promised in advance.
Believing after something happens that you knew it all along. It makes people overconfident about predicting the future.
When a company that mainly owns shares in other companies trades below the combined value of those holdings. Investors apply it because they cannot control or easily access the underlying value.

How long you own an asset before selling it. In Pakistan, capital gains tax on property and securities has at times depended on the holding period, and these rules change, so check the latest Finance Act.
Putting too much money into familiar local investments, like only Pakistani property or one known company, and missing diversification.
Bank financing to buy, build or renovate a house, offered in conventional and Islamic forms, repaid in monthly instalments over many years.
Short-term foreign money that moves into a country to chase high interest rates or quick gains and leaves just as fast. Sudden exits can hit the currency and markets.

An informal, unregulated way of moving money between countries outside the banking system. It is illegal in Pakistan, can be linked to money laundering, and offers no protection if the money disappears.
A REIT that combines rental properties and development projects in one fund.
Extremely fast and out-of-control price rises, where money loses value within weeks or months. It usually follows a collapse in trust in the currency.
A standard bank account number that includes the country code, check digits, bank code and account number. Pakistani IBANs start with 'PK' and are 24 characters long.
A way to send money instantly from one bank account to another bank through apps, internet banking or ATMs.

An Islamic lease where the bank owns an asset and rents it out for a fixed period and rent. The owner bears major ownership risks, and the asset may be transferred to the customer at the end by a separate agreement.
example: Islamic car financing where the bank owns the car and the customer pays monthly rent.

definition: A housing project marketed to the public without approval from the development authority. Buyers can lose their money or never get legal title.
A share that trades rarely or in small amounts. It can be hard to sell when you want, and a single order can move its price a lot.

A loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund, usually when a country is short of foreign currency. The money comes in instalments tied to conditions such as raising taxes, cutting deficits and reforming energy prices.
A periodic check by the IMF on whether a country has met the programme's conditions. Passing it usually releases the next loan instalment, which markets often treat as good news.
Reducing the recorded value of an asset when it is found to be worth less than its book value. It lowers profit in that period.
How many months of imports a country could pay for using its foreign exchange reserves. Low import cover is a warning sign for the currency.
example: Reserves of USD 9 billion with imports of USD 4.5 billion a month give about 2 months of import cover.

definition: A fund that invests in debt such as government securities, TFCs, sukuk and bank deposits to earn interest or profit. It is riskier than a money market fund because it can hold longer and lower-rated debt.
A report showing a company's revenue, costs and profit or loss over a period.
A yearly declaration to the FBR of your income, taxes already deducted, and tax payable or refundable. Filing it is what makes you a filer.
A fund that simply copies a market index by holding the same shares in the same proportions. It does not try to beat the market, so its fees are usually low.
A cash-settled futures contract based on a stock index rather than one company. PSX has offered index futures on the KSE-30.

The unit in which an index level and its daily change are expressed. A rise of 500 points means something different depending on how high the index already is, so percentage change is often more useful.
The regular review where the exchange adds or removes companies from an index and updates their weights. PSX reviews its indices on a set schedule.
A tax included in the price of goods and services and passed on to the buyer, such as sales tax or customs duty. Everyone pays it when they buy, regardless of income.
The general rise in prices over time, which means each rupee buys less than before. It is usually reported as a yearly percentage change in a price index such as the CPI.
example: If a bag of flour costs Rs 1,000 this year and Rs 1,100 next year, its price has inflated by 10%.

definition: The risk that inflation grows faster than your return, so your money buys less in future.
Business activity that is not recorded or taxed, often done in cash. A large informal economy keeps tax revenue low.
The deposit required before you can open a leveraged or futures position. It is set as a portion of the trade value.
Important facts about a company that are not yet public and would likely move its share price if known.
Buying or selling shares using important company information that the public does not yet know. It is illegal in Pakistan and punished by SECP.
When a person or company cannot pay its debts as they fall due. Shareholders are usually paid last, if at all.
A fixed regular payment, usually monthly, that repays a loan or purchase over time.
Buying a plot or flat from a developer by paying in instalments while it is being built. You take the risk that the developer delays or fails to deliver.
A large organisation that invests on behalf of others, such as mutual funds, banks, insurance companies and pension funds. Their trades are big enough to move prices.
A contract where you pay regular amounts to a company that agrees to pay you or your family if a specific loss or event happens. Insurers in Pakistan are regulated by SECP.
A free, independent office that handles complaints against insurance companies that are not resolved by the insurer.
Valuable things without physical form, such as software, licences, brands and patents.
The exchange rate at which banks trade foreign currency with each other in large amounts. It is the main official market rate for the rupee.
Operating profit divided by finance cost. It shows how many times a company can pay its interest from profits; a low number is a danger sign.
example: Operating profit of PKR 40 crore and finance cost of PKR 10 crore give interest cover of 4 times.

definition: The band SBP sets around the policy rate. The top is the rate at which banks can borrow overnight from SBP, and the bottom is the rate SBP pays banks on overnight deposits, which keeps market rates close to the policy rate.
The risk that a bond or debt fund falls in value because interest rates rise.
A dividend paid during the financial year, often after quarterly or half-yearly results, before the full-year accounts are final. The board can announce it without waiting for the annual meeting.
An estimate of what a share is really worth based on the business's future earnings or cash, regardless of today's market price. Different analysts can reach different figures.
Goods a company holds for sale, along with raw materials and partly made products. Pakistani accounts often call it stock-in-trade.
Roughly how many days of sales a company keeps as stock. Rising inventory days can mean goods are not selling well.
A yield curve where short-term yields are higher than long-term yields, often a sign the market expects interest rates to fall.
Putting money into assets expected to produce income or grow in value over time, after understanding the risks. It is usually long-term, unlike speculation.
Cash spent on or received from long-term assets and investments, such as buying machines or selling property.
Your account with an AMC that records the units you own across its funds. You open it once after KYC and use it for all purchases and redemptions.
A group of senior people at an AMC who set and review investment decisions and limits for its funds.
Credit ratings of BBB- and above, meaning default risk is judged acceptable for careful investors.
An account held directly with CDC instead of through a broker. Your shares stay under your own control, and you move them to a broker only when you want to sell.
When a company sells its shares to the public for the first time and gets listed on the stock exchange. In Pakistan, IPOs are approved by SECP and PSX.
An account opened with a bank to hold government securities like T-bills and PIBs in your name electronically.
The FBR's online portal for registering as a taxpayer and filing income tax returns and wealth statements. Individuals log in to file their yearly return.
Banking that follows Shariah, using contracts like Mudarabah, Musharakah, Murabaha and Ijarah instead of interest. Some conventional banks offer it through separate Islamic branches or windows.

The rules of Islamic law that fix what share of a deceased Muslim's estate each heir receives. A will (wasiyat) generally can only cover up to one third of the estate and not for heirs who already get a share.
A contract to make or build something to a set specification for an agreed price, with payment possible in stages. It is used for construction and manufacturing finance.
An account owned by two or more people. Operating terms decide whether one person alone can withdraw or all must sign.
A measure of gold purity out of 24 parts. 24-karat gold is nearly pure, while 22-karat gold is about 91.6% gold mixed with other metals for strength.
example: A 21-karat ring weighing 1 tola contains about 21/24 of a tola of pure gold.

definition: A short, standard summary of the most important facts about a financial product, like fees, risks and returns, so customers can compare products easily. Banks, AMCs and insurers provide these.
A benchmark rate based on what banks say they would charge to lend to each other for set periods. Many loans and TFCs in Pakistan are priced as KIBOR plus a margin.
example: A business loan at 6-month KIBOR + 2% costs 14% if KIBOR is a made-up 12%.

definition: A PSX index that includes all listed companies that pass Shariah screening criteria. It gives a broad view of the Islamic segment of the market.
A PSX index of 30 Shariah-compliant companies, created jointly with Al Meezan Investments. It is the main benchmark for Islamic equity investing in Pakistan.
The checks a bank, AMC or broker must do to confirm who you are and where your money comes from before opening an account. It helps stop fraud and money laundering.

Pakistan's main stock market index, tracking 100 companies chosen mainly by market size, with rules so major sectors are represented. It is free-float weighted and is the most quoted measure of how PSX is doing.
A PSX index of 30 large and highly traded companies, weighted by free float. It focuses on liquid shares and is also used as the base for index futures.
The identity and background checks a broker must do before opening your account, such as verifying your CNIC and source of income. It helps prevent fraud and money laundering.
When a policy stops because premiums were not paid even after the grace period. Cover ends, though it can sometimes be revived.
A share of a company with a very large market capitalisation. These tend to be more established and less volatile than smaller companies.
A Pakistani index that tracks output from big factories in sectors like textiles, cement, food, cars and steel. It is a monthly clue to how industry is doing.
A PSX term for a share's closing price on the previous trading day. Today's change and daily price limits are measured from it.
example: If LDCP is PKR 80 and the share now trades at PKR 84, it is up PKR 4 or 5%.

definition: The amount a company owes under long-term rental agreements for assets like buildings or vehicles, recorded as a debt under accounting rules.
A person entitled by law to inherit from someone who has died, such as a spouse, children or parents. For Muslims in Pakistan, shares are generally fixed by Islamic inheritance rules.
A legal document allowing someone to manage and distribute a deceased person's estate, often covering immovable property, when there is no will or executor.
Using borrowed money to buy more investments than your own cash allows. It magnifies gains and losses alike.
example: With PKR 1 lakh of your own and PKR 1 lakh borrowed, a 10% drop costs you 20% of your own money.

definition: Amounts a company owes to others, such as loans, money owed to suppliers, taxes and other obligations.
Money you owe to others, such as loans, credit card balances or unpaid bills.
A VPS allocation that automatically moves money from shares toward safer debt and cash as you get closer to retirement age.
When spending rises every time income rises, so you never save more even as you earn more.
An order to buy or sell only at a set price or better. It protects you from bad prices but may not fill if the market never reaches your price.
example: You place a buy limit at PKR 48; it only fills if a seller is willing to sell at PKR 48 or less.

definition: A simple chart joining closing prices with a line to show the overall trend.
Data showing net buying or selling by local investor groups like banks, mutual funds, insurers, companies and individuals on PSX. It is published alongside FIPI.
How easily a share can be bought or sold quickly without moving its price much. Shares with high daily volume and tight spreads are liquid.
The risk that you cannot sell an investment quickly at a fair price when you need cash.
Being admitted to trade on a stock exchange. Listed companies must follow exchange rules, publish accounts and disclose important news.
How long you have to repay a loan. Longer tenures mean smaller instalments but more total cost.
Owning a share or contract because you expect its price to rise. You profit if the price goes up.
Loans repayable over more than a year, often used to fund new plants or expansions.
Holding investments for many years and riding out short-term ups and downs to benefit from growth and compounding.
Feeling the pain of a loss much more strongly than the joy of an equal gain. It can make people hold losing investments too long or avoid sensible risks.
When a share falls to the lowest price allowed for the day. Sellers pile up with few buyers, so it can be hard to exit that day.
Investing a large amount all at once rather than spreading it over time. It puts money to work sooner but carries the risk of investing right before a fall.
An indicator built from the gap between two exponential moving averages, plus a signal line. Crossovers between the lines are used to spot changes in momentum.

The extra cost jewellers add for crafting jewellery, plus any deduction they may take when you sell it back. Because of these, jewellery is a more costly way to invest in gold than plain bars or coins.
An exchange-rate system where the currency mostly moves with market forces but the central bank can step in to smooth large swings.
The fee an AMC charges a fund for managing its money, set as a yearly percentage of net assets and charged daily through the NAV. It is the largest part of the TER for most funds.
A rating that judges how well an AMC is run, including its controls, people and processes, rather than any single fund.
The money or shares you must deposit as security when trading with borrowed funds or in futures. It protects the lender or clearing house if prices move against you.
A demand from your broker to deposit more money because your losses have reduced your margin below the required level. If you do not pay, your positions can be sold.
Borrowing from a broker or financier to buy shares, putting up part of the cost yourself as margin. If prices fall, you must add more money or your shares may be sold.
Buying a share well below your estimate of its intrinsic value, so you are protected if your estimate is wrong.
example: If you value a share at PKR 100 and buy at PKR 70, your margin of safety is 30%.

definition: A Pakistani system run by NCCPL where a financier pays part of the cost of your share purchase and earns a financing fee, while the shares are kept as security. It lets traders buy more shares than their cash alone allows, which raises risk.
The tax rate on your next rupee of income. It is usually higher than your average rate because of slabs.
Revaluing open positions at the latest market price every day. Gains are credited and losses must be paid in, usually daily.
example: If your futures contract loses PKR 5,000 in value today, that amount is taken from your margin account.

definition: The total market value of a company's shares. It equals the share price multiplied by the total number of shares.
example: 100 crore shares at PKR 50 each gives a market cap of PKR 5,000 crore.

definition: A sudden and very large fall in share prices, usually driven by panic. Crashes can wipe out a big part of market value in days.
How many shares are waiting to be bought or sold at prices near the current price. Good depth means large orders can be filled without moving the price much.
A temporary stop to all trading, triggered when the main index moves sharply within a short time. PSX can halt trading this way to slow down panic selling or buying.
The standard number of shares in which a stock trades in the normal market. The exchange sets the lot size and may change it.
Illegally creating false prices or fake trading activity to mislead other investors. SECP and PSX monitor and penalise it.
An order to buy or sell immediately at the best price available right now. It fills fast, but the exact price can be worse than you expected if the market moves.
example: You place a market order for 100 shares and get them at PKR 50.10 even though the last trade showed PKR 50.

definition: The overall mood of investors, whether optimistic or fearful. Sentiment can push prices up or down in the short term regardless of company fundamentals.
Trying to buy just before prices rise and sell just before they fall. It is very hard to do consistently, and missing a few good days can greatly reduce returns.
The cost of borrowing from a bank, charged as a yearly percentage. Pakistani banks commonly use the word markup instead of interest.
Company news that could affect its share price, such as results, dividends, big contracts or legal problems. Listed companies must announce it to PSX promptly.
The date when a bond, deposit or certificate ends and the principal is repaid.
The amount an endowment or savings policy pays if the insured person survives to the end of the term.
The total amount you receive when a deposit or certificate ends, including principal and any profit not already paid.
The largest peak-to-low fall an investment suffered over a period. It helps you judge whether you could stomach the worst case.
Gambling or pure speculation where one side's gain depends on chance and the other's loss. It is prohibited in Islamic finance.
Treating money differently depending on where it came from or which mental 'bucket' it is in, even though all money is the same.
example: Spending a Rs 50,000 bonus freely while carrying a costly credit card balance.

definition: When two companies combine into one. Shareholders of the company that disappears usually receive shares of the combined company at a set ratio.
A share of a medium-sized company by market capitalisation. They can grow faster than large caps but carry more risk.
Extra tax or spending changes made in the middle of a fiscal year, outside the main budget. It often happens when revenue falls short or a lender asks for new measures.
The smallest amount a credit card company requires you to pay each month. Paying only this keeps the account in good standing but leaves the rest of the balance growing with high charges.
example: Paying Rs 5,000 a month on a Rs 200,000 card balance could take years to clear because most of it goes to charges.

definition: The lowest profit rate SBP requires conventional banks to pay on savings deposits, linked to the SBP policy framework so savers get a fair share when rates rise.
A tax that must be paid even if your calculated tax liability is lower, often based on turnover or deducted on certain transactions. It cannot be fully refunded even if you had a loss.
Selling a financial product by hiding or misstating its risks, costs or nature, such as presenting an insurance plan as a fixed deposit.
The approximate percentage change in a bond's price for a 1 percentage point change in yield.
