example: With a modified duration of 4, a 1% rise in yields cuts the price by about 4%.

definition: The speed and strength of a price move. Momentum traders buy shares that are rising strongly, betting the move continues.
When the central bank cuts interest rates to support growth. Savings returns fall, loans get cheaper, and shares often benefit.
Actions by the central bank to control inflation and support the economy, mainly by setting interest rates. In Pakistan this is done by the State Bank of Pakistan.
The SBP committee that meets on a published schedule to decide the policy rate and explain its view of the economy.
The announcement SBP releases after an MPC meeting stating the policy rate decision and the reasons behind it.
When the central bank raises interest rates or reduces money supply to cool inflation. It tends to slow borrowing and can weigh on share prices.
Hiding the criminal source of money by passing it through banks, businesses, property or investments so it looks clean. It is a serious crime.

A low-risk fund that invests in very short-term, high-quality instruments such as T-bills, bank deposits and short sukuk. It aims for steady returns and quick access to cash, and is often used instead of a savings account.
example: Parking PKR 200,000 emergency savings in a money market fund that can be redeemed in a day or two.

definition: The total amount of money in an economy, including cash and bank deposits. Money supply growing much faster than output can feed inflation.
When someone takes bigger risks because they expect others to bear the losses, such as a company expecting a government bailout.
The charge deducted for the life cover itself, based on your age and the risk of death.
A loan to buy property, where the property itself is the collateral. If you stop paying, the lender can take the property.
The average closing price over a set number of recent days, recalculated daily. It smooths out daily noise to show the trend.
example: The 50-day moving average is the average close of the last 50 trading days.

definition: A partnership where one side provides money and the other provides work and skill. Profit is shared at an agreed ratio, while any money loss falls on the provider of capital unless the worker was negligent. Islamic savings accounts are often based on it.
example: A depositor (capital provider) and the bank (manager) agree to share pool profit 60:40.

definition: The party that manages the money and runs the business in a Mudarabah, such as the bank managing depositors' funds.
The industry body of Pakistan's AMCs. It publishes daily NAVs, returns and fund categories, and sets standards for its members.

Standard groups used to classify Pakistani funds, such as money market, income, aggressive income, equity, balanced, asset allocation, fund of funds, capital protected, index tracker, commodity, ETF and VPS. Each usually has a conventional and a Shariah compliant version.
A sale where the bank buys an asset and sells it to the customer at its cost plus a disclosed profit, often paid in instalments. The price is fixed once agreed.
example: A bank buys raw material for PKR 1,000,000 and sells it to a business for PKR 1,100,000 payable in six months.

definition: A joint partnership where all partners put in money and share profit at an agreed ratio, while losses are shared in proportion to each partner's capital.
Updating the official land revenue record to show a new owner after a sale, gift or inheritance.

A pool of money collected from many investors and invested by professionals in shares, bonds, bank deposits or other assets. Each investor owns units and shares in the gains and losses in proportion to the units held.
example: Ali puts PKR 50,000 into an income fund and receives 500 units at PKR 100 each.

definition: Short selling without first arranging to borrow the shares. It is generally not permitted in Pakistan because the seller may be unable to deliver.
The company that clears and settles trades on PSX, making sure money and shares change hands correctly. It also calculates and collects capital gains tax on listed securities.
The formula that decides how federal tax revenue is shared between the federal government and the provinces. It affects how much money each level of government has to spend.
Government savings products sold by CDNS through National Savings Centres and some banks. They are backed by the Government of Pakistan, so default risk is very low.
A CDNS savings account that pays variable profit and allows withdrawals, similar to a bank savings account but backed by the government.
A unique number given by the FBR to identify a taxpayer. For individuals in Pakistan, the CNIC number is generally used as the NTN.
Total assets minus total liabilities, divided by the number of shares or units. For investment companies and funds it is usually based on the market value of their holdings.
Government savings certificates for Roshan Digital Account holders, offered in USD and PKR, with conventional and Islamic versions.

aka: National Clearing Company of Pakistan Limited
definition: The company that clears and settles PSX trades, making sure buyers get shares and sellers get money. It also runs financing systems like MTS and handles capital gains tax calculation on listed securities.
A PSX segment where large pre-agreed trades between two parties are reported and executed. It lets big investors swap large blocks without disturbing the normal market price.
The value of one unit of a fund, worked out as (total value of the fund's assets minus its liabilities) divided by the number of units. Open-end funds in Pakistan announce NAV every business day.
example: Assets PKR 1,050 million minus liabilities PKR 50 million, divided by 10 million units, gives a NAV of PKR 100.

definition: Total borrowings minus cash and cash equivalents. If cash is larger than debt, the company has net cash.
Net profit as a percentage of sales. It shows how much of each rupee of sales finally becomes profit for shareholders.
The profit left after all costs, interest and taxes. It is the amount that belongs to shareholders.
Everything you own minus everything you owe. It is a snapshot of your overall financial position.
example: Assets of Rs 5,000,000 minus loans of Rs 1,500,000 gives a net worth of Rs 3,500,000.

definition: A unique digital token recording ownership of a digital item such as art. NFT prices are highly speculative and many have lost most of their value.
The minimum amount of wealth, measured against a value of gold or silver, above which Zakat becomes due.

An official approval stating that an authority has no objection to something, such as a housing scheme being launched or a property being transferred. Buying in a scheme without the required NOC is very risky.
The return on an investment before adjusting for inflation. It is the raw percentage you see on a statement.
example: Rs 100,000 growing to Rs 112,000 is a 12% nominal return.

definition: A person you name to receive money from an account, policy or certificate if you die. The nominee may hold it for the legal heirs.
An auction bid that states only the amount and accepts whatever yield the auction sets. It lets smaller investors take part without guessing the rate.
The part of a subsidiary owned by outside shareholders rather than the parent company, shown separately in consolidated accounts.
Assets a company keeps for more than a year, such as land, factories, machinery and long-term investments.
Obligations due after more than a year, such as long-term loans, lease liabilities and deferred tax.

A person not on the Active Taxpayers List. Non-filers usually face higher withholding taxes on things like bank withdrawals, property, vehicles and investment income, and may face other restrictions. The exact rates and rules change, so check with FBR.
The standard system where all your taxable income is added together and taxed at slab rates, with taxes already paid adjusted against the total.
A yield curve where long-term bonds pay more than short-term ones, the usual case because lenders want more for tying money up longer.
A quantity of shares smaller than the standard market lot. PSX lets odd lots be traded in a separate odd-lot segment, often with fewer buyers and sellers.
example: Bonus shares sometimes leave you with an odd number like 37 shares, which may need to be sold as an odd lot.

definition: When existing owners sell some of their shares to the public. The company itself receives no new money, unlike when it issues fresh shares.
The price you pay to buy one unit of a fund. It equals the NAV plus any front-end load.
example: NAV PKR 100 with a 2% front-end load gives an offer price of PKR 102.

definition: The official legal document of a fund that explains its objective, allowed investments, risks, fees, loads and how to buy and redeem. It should be read before investing.
The four key prices for a period: the opening price, highest price, lowest price and closing price. Charts and daily market reports are built from these numbers.
A PSX index of selected liquid oil and gas sector shares, designed so funds and ETFs can track the energy sector.
The global price of crude oil, often tracked by the Brent benchmark. As a big fuel importer, Pakistan's import bill, inflation and rupee are sensitive to oil prices.
An independent official who handles public complaints against institutions for free. Pakistan has ombudsmen for banking, tax, insurance and federal government bodies.
An open market operation in which SBP lends cash to banks, adding money to the system when it is short.
An open market operation in which SBP takes extra cash out of the banking system.
An unusual gain or loss that is not expected to repeat, such as a big asset sale or a court settlement. Investors often exclude it to judge normal earnings.
The total number of futures or options contracts still open and not yet closed or settled. Rising open interest shows more money entering that contract.
SBP buying or selling securities, often through short repos, to add cash to or remove cash from the banking system and keep overnight rates near the policy rate.
The exchange rate at licensed exchange companies where individuals buy and sell cash foreign currency. A big gap between this and the interbank rate can signal stress or shortages of dollars.
A fund that issues new units and buys back units on any dealing day at NAV-based prices. Its size grows or shrinks as investors come and go. Most Pakistani mutual funds are open-end.
Cash generated by the company's normal business activities. A healthy company usually produces operating cash flow close to or above its net profit.
Day-to-day costs of running the business beyond making the product, such as selling, distribution, salaries and office costs.
Operating profit as a percentage of sales. It shows how efficiently the core business is run.
Profit from the main business after operating expenses but before interest and tax. EBIT stands for earnings before interest and taxes.
What you give up by choosing one option over another. Money kept idle has the opportunity cost of returns it could have earned elsewhere.
example: Keeping Rs 1,000,000 in a zero-profit current account means missing the profit a savings option could have paid.

definition: A contract giving the buyer the right, but not the duty, to buy (call) or sell (put) an asset at a set price before a set date. The buyer pays a fee called a premium.
An instruction you give your broker to buy or sell a certain number of shares. It may include a price limit and how long it should stay active.
The live list of all waiting buy and sell orders for a share, arranged by price. It shows how much demand and supply sits at each price level.
A decision at a shareholder meeting that needs a simple majority of votes, such as approving accounts or dividends.
Income from activities outside the main business, such as interest on bank deposits, dividends or gains on selling assets. It can make profits look better than the core business is doing.
When a price has risen so fast that indicators suggest it may be due for a pause or pullback. It is a warning, not a guarantee.
Believing you know more or can predict better than you really can. It leads to trading too often, taking too much risk and skipping diversification.
A facility that lets you take out more than your account balance up to a limit, paying markup only on the amount used.
The rate at which banks lend to each other for one day. SBP tries to keep it near the policy rate.
When a price has fallen so fast that indicators suggest it may be due for a bounce. Prices can still keep falling.
When investors apply for more shares than are on offer in an IPO or right issue. Shares are then allotted in part, by ballot or by a set formula.
example: If 1 crore shares are offered and applications come for 3 crore, the issue is 3 times oversubscribed.

definition: When a share's market price is above what an investor believes it is truly worth.
A policy where you stop paying premiums but keep reduced cover based on what you have already paid, instead of surrendering it.
The government agency that publishes official data such as CPI, SPI, trade figures and the census. It is the primary source for Pakistan's inflation numbers.
A yearly report from the Ministry of Finance released before the budget, reviewing growth, inflation, trade, debt and other parts of the economy.
A longer-term government bond lasting several years that pays coupons, usually every six months, and returns face value at maturity.
Pakistan's regulated commodity exchange, where contracts on things like gold, oil and other commodities and financial products are traded. These are mostly leveraged products that carry high risk.
Pakistan's national stock exchange, where shares, ETFs, bonds and futures of listed companies are bought and sold. It was formed by merging the Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad exchanges.
Selling investments in fear during a sharp fall, often locking in losses just before prices recover.
The pool, often set up as a waqf (charitable trust), into which participants' contributions go and from which claims are paid. It belongs to the participants, not the operator.
Aiming to match the market by holding a broad index-tracking investment at low cost, rather than trying to beat it.
A cheque issued by a bank itself, payable in the same city, so the receiver knows the money is guaranteed.
A habit of moving a set amount into savings or investments as soon as you get paid, before spending on anything else.
Roughly how many days a company takes to pay its suppliers.
Valuing a company by comparing its ratios, such as P/E or P/B, with similar companies in the same sector.
Buying or selling crypto directly with another person, often paying through bank transfer or mobile wallet. It carries risks of fraud and of receiving funds linked to crime.
P/E divided by the expected yearly earnings growth rate. A PEG near or below 1 can suggest the price is reasonable for the growth on offer.
example: A P/E of 10 with 20% expected growth gives a PEG of 0.5.

definition: A very low-priced share, often of a small or weak company. Such shares are cheap per unit but can be very risky and easy to manipulate.
A fund built to save for retirement. In Pakistan's VPS, each pension fund is split into sub-funds like equity, debt and money market.
A National Savings account for retired government and other pensioners that pays monthly profit, usually at a favourable rate.
A country's total income divided by its population. It gives a rough idea of the average living standard.
A plan for how you will spend and save your money each month. It helps you see where money goes and find room to save and invest.
example: From a Rs 150,000 salary, Ali plans Rs 90,000 for needs, Rs 30,000 for wants and Rs 30,000 for savings.

definition: A loan from a bank or lender for personal use without needing collateral. It usually carries a higher rate than secured loans.
A per-litre charge the government adds to petrol and diesel prices to raise revenue. Its level changes over time and is often linked to budget or IMF targets.
Shares held as paper certificates instead of electronically in CDC. In Pakistan they must be converted into electronic form before they can be sold on PSX.

A document in a housing scheme that gives the right to a plot that has not yet been identified or delivered. Files are popular for speculation but risky, because the scheme may be unapproved, delayed or may sell more files than it has land.

The traditional Pakistani name for a savings account that earns profit on the balance. The term comes from banks' shift to profit-based deposits, but conventional PLS accounts today simply pay a variable profit rate.
The main interest rate set by the State Bank of Pakistan to control inflation and growth. Bank deposit, loan and bond rates tend to move with it.
The person who owns an insurance policy and pays the premiums.
The risk that political events, such as protests, elections or sudden policy changes, hurt the economy or investments.

Someone who holds or has held an important public position, like a senior politician, judge or military officer, plus close family and associates. Banks and brokers apply extra checks to PEPs because of higher corruption risk.
A fraud that pays old investors with money from new investors instead of real profits. It collapses when new money stops, and most people lose their money.
example: A scheme promising a guaranteed 10% a month that pays only as long as more people join is a classic Ponzi.

definition: The combined deposits an Islamic bank invests together. The pool's actual earnings are calculated each period and shared between depositors and the bank.
The full collection of investments you own, such as shares, funds, gold and savings certificates.
Physically receiving the property so you can build on it or live in it. Many schemes sell plots long before possession is possible.

A legal document that lets someone act on your behalf, such as selling property or operating an account. It is powerful and can be misused, so only give it to people you fully trust and limit its scope.
A short period before normal trading starts when orders can be entered to help find a fair opening price. Trades are matched when the regular session begins.
Taking money out of a term deposit or savings certificate before maturity. It usually earns a lower rate or a penalty.
The amount you pay, monthly, yearly or once, to keep an insurance policy active.
example: Paying PKR 30,000 a year for life cover of PKR 3,000,000.

definition: When a bond's market price is higher than its face value, usually because its coupon is higher than current market rates.
example: A PKR 100 bond trading at PKR 104 is at a PKR 4 premium.

definition: The amount above face value that a company charges for new right shares.
example: Right shares with PKR 10 face value offered at PKR 25 carry a PKR 15 premium.

definition: A prize bond registered in the buyer's name that pays regular profit and also enters prize draws. Registration makes it safer than bearer bonds because only the owner can cash it.
Paying off some or all of a loan before its due date. It saves future charges, but some lenders charge a fee for it.
What a future amount of money is worth today after discounting it.
example: At a made-up 10% discount rate, PKR 110 received in one year is worth PKR 100 today.

definition: The allowed range within which bids can be placed during book building, from the floor price up to an upper limit.
How much a share's price has moved compared to the previous close, shown in rupees and as a percentage.
Share price divided by book value per share. A P/B below 1 means the share trades for less than its accounting value, which can signal a bargain or deep problems.
example: A PKR 40 share with breakup value of PKR 50 has a P/B of 0.8.

definition: Share price divided by EPS. It shows how many rupees investors pay for each rupee of yearly profit; a lower P/E can mean cheaper, but may also signal problems.
example: A PKR 60 share with EPS of PKR 10 has a P/E of 6.

definition: Market cap divided by yearly sales. It is useful for valuing companies with low or negative profits.

aka: Inverse Relationship of Price and Yield
definition: Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions. When interest rates rise, existing bonds fall in price, and when rates fall, their prices rise.
The government's budget balance after leaving out interest payments on debt. A primary surplus means the government covers its non-interest spending from revenue.
A bank or financial institution appointed by SBP to bid directly in government securities auctions and help keep the market active. Others usually buy through them.
Where securities are first sold by the issuer, such as a government auction or an IPO.
The original money you invest or lend, before any profit, interest or loss.
Putting money into a business that is not listed on a stock exchange, such as a friend's shop or startup. It can pay well but is hard to sell and needs clear written agreements.
A secret code that proves ownership of crypto in a wallet. Anyone who gets it can take your coins, and if you lose it the coins are usually gone forever; never share it.
A government bond sold by CDNS and SBP that pays no profit but enters the holder into regular prize draws. The face value can be cashed at any time.
example: A PKR 750 bond either wins a prize in a draw or can be encashed later for PKR 750.

definition: A public lottery-style draw held on a schedule where bond numbers are picked to win prizes. Winners claim prizes, after tax, from designated offices or banks.
Profit after all expenses including finance cost, but before income tax.
A reserve an Islamic bank builds from pool income in good periods to smooth depositors' returns in weak periods.
How often profit is credited to an account or certificate, such as monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or at maturity.
The yearly percentage a bank pays on deposits. Islamic banks call it an expected or declared profit rate because it comes from pool earnings.
The pre-agreed split of actual profit between partners in Mudarabah or Musharakah, such as between depositors and the Islamic bank. It must be a ratio of profit, never a fixed amount.
example: With a 70:30 ratio, a PKR 10,000 profit gives PKR 7,000 to depositors and PKR 3,000 to the bank.

definition: Selling shares after a price rise to lock in gains. Heavy profit-taking can cause prices to dip after a rally.
A tax where higher incomes pay a higher percentage. Pakistan's personal income tax is progressive.
A middleman who connects buyers and sellers of property for a commission. Always verify documents yourself instead of relying only on the dealer.

Official values set for property in different areas, used to calculate taxes and duties on property deals. The FBR and provincial district collectors publish their own rates, which may differ from the actual market price.
Physical long-term assets like land, buildings, machines and vehicles used to run the business.
The official document a company publishes before an IPO describing its business, finances, risks and how the money raised will be used. Read it before applying.
A retirement savings fund where an employee and often the employer contribute part of the salary each month, paid out with profit on leaving or retiring.
A provincial body that collects sales tax on services and other provincial taxes, such as the Sindh Revenue Board or Punjab Revenue Authority.
Reducing the recorded value of a debt holding in a fund when the borrower stops paying or is likely to. It lowers the NAV.
Amounts set aside for likely future costs whose exact size or timing is uncertain, such as legal claims or bad debts.
A person you appoint to attend and vote on your behalf at a shareholder meeting.
A PSX index of 20 companies selected for their dividend record and yield. It tracks high-dividend paying shares.
All money the government owes, both to lenders inside the country and abroad. It is often compared to GDP to judge whether it is manageable.
An offer to buy shares directly from all public shareholders, often at a set price. Pakistani takeover law requires an acquirer to make such an offer when buying a large controlling stake.
The part of the federal budget set aside for development projects like roads, dams and schools. It is often cut when the government needs to reduce its deficit.
A short, temporary price dip within a larger uptrend, or a short rise within a downtrend.
A scam where people hype a share with rumours to push its price up, then sell their own holdings to those who bought late. Prices then collapse.
How much goods and services a sum of money can buy. Inflation reduces purchasing power over time.
Giving to charity the small part of income or dividends that came from non-compliant sources, so the remaining return is Shariah compliant. Islamic funds report a purification amount.
example: If 2% of a company's income is non-compliant, 2% of the dividend received is given to charity.

definition: A Pakistani authority set up to regulate and license virtual asset service providers such as crypto exchanges. Its rules are new and evolving, so check its official announcements.
A scheme where people earn mainly by recruiting others who pay to join, rather than by selling a real product. Most participants lose money and such schemes can be illegal.
An interest-free loan that must be repaid in the same amount. Current accounts in Islamic banks are usually treated as Qard to the bank.
An auditor's report saying the accounts are fair except for specific problems. It is a warning sign worth reading carefully.
Comparing a figure with the previous quarter. It shows short-term momentum but can be affected by seasons.
Financial results covering three months. Pakistani listed companies publish results for the first quarter, half-year, nine months and full year.
Like the current ratio, but leaves out inventory because it may be hard to sell fast. It is a stricter test of short-term safety.
SBP's instant payment system that moves money between banks and wallets in seconds. You can send money using an IBAN or a Raast ID.
A simple alias, normally your mobile number, linked to your bank account so people can send you money through Raast without your IBAN.
The investor who supplies the money in a Mudarabah.
A period of strong and fairly quick price increases in a share or the whole market.
A note with a rating, such as positive, stable or negative, showing which way the rating might move in future.
PSX's normal market for buying and selling shares, where trades settle on the standard settlement cycle and actual shares are delivered. Most retail trading happens here.
An interest rate minus inflation. A positive real rate means savers are being rewarded above price rises; a negative one means savers are losing buying power.
Your return after removing the effect of inflation. It shows whether your buying power actually grew.
example: Earning 12% when inflation is 9% gives a real return of roughly 3%.

definition: Bringing your portfolio back to its target mix by selling some of what has grown too large and buying what has shrunk. It keeps your risk level where you intended.
example: If shares grow from 60% to 75% of your portfolio, you sell some and buy other assets to return to 60%.

definition: Roughly how many days customers take to pay. Long receivable days tie up cash and raise the risk of bad debts.
Assuming that what happened recently will keep happening, such as expecting a rising market to keep rising forever.
A significant fall in economic activity lasting months, with lower output, jobs and spending. A common rule of thumb is two quarters in a row of shrinking GDP.
The date on which a company checks its records to decide who is eligible for a corporate action. You must be a recorded shareholder by then.
After a loss, you need a bigger percentage gain just to get back to where you started. Formula: gain needed = loss / (1 - loss).
example: After a 50% loss, Rs 100,000 becomes Rs 50,000 and needs a 100% gain to return to Rs 100,000.

definition: Selling your fund units back to the AMC to get cash. Money usually reaches your bank account within a few working days.
The price you receive per unit when you sell units back to the fund. It equals the NAV minus any back-end load.
example: NAV PKR 100 with a 1% back-end load gives a redemption price of PKR 99.

definition: The sale deed registered with the sub-registrar that legally records the transfer of property from seller to buyer, after paying applicable taxes and stamp duty.
Avoiding decisions out of fear of regretting them later, which can lead to doing nothing or following the crowd.
National Savings certificates that pay profit every month, built for people who want a steady monthly income from their savings.
example: PKR 1,000,000 at a made-up 12% gives about PKR 10,000 a month before tax.

definition: The risk that coupons or matured money can only be reinvested at lower rates than before.

A fund that owns or develops real estate and lets investors buy units, often listed on the stock exchange. It allows you to invest in property with small amounts and sell more easily than a physical property. In Pakistan REITs are regulated by SECP.

Deals between the company and people or businesses connected to it, such as sponsors, directors or group companies. They must be disclosed because they can be used to shift value away from minority shareholders.
A momentum indicator from 0 to 100 that compares recent gains with recent losses. Readings above about 70 are often called overbought and below about 30 oversold.
Money sent home by people working abroad. For Pakistan they are a major source of foreign currency and help cover the trade deficit.
example: A worker in Dubai sending Rs 80,000 a month to his family in Sialkot through a bank is sending remittances.

definition: To give up or transfer your right to buy right shares to someone else, often by selling the right letter.
Yearly rent as a percentage of the property's price. Formula: rent yield = yearly rent / property value x 100.
example: A flat worth Rs 20,000,000 renting for Rs 80,000 a month earns Rs 960,000 a year, a 4.8% gross yield.

definition: A REIT that owns completed, income-producing buildings like malls or offices and passes most of the rental income to unit holders.

A short-term loan where one party sells securities and agrees to buy them back later at a slightly higher price. The difference is the interest. Banks use repos to borrow cash against government securities.
Parts of equity built up from retained profits, share premium or revaluations. They show accumulated value kept in the business.
Houses, flats and plots meant for people to live in.
A price level where a rising share has tended to stall because sellers appear. It acts like a ceiling until it is broken.
An ordinary person investing their own money, usually in smaller amounts than institutions.
The part of an IPO set aside for ordinary individual investors, separate from the part offered to large investors in book building.
Profits the company has kept over the years instead of paying out as dividends. Pakistani accounts commonly call this unappropriated profit.
Takaful for takaful operators, where they pass part of their large risks to another Shariah compliant provider.
The share of profit kept in the business instead of being paid as dividends. It equals 1 minus the payout ratio.
Preparing to have enough savings and income to live on after you stop working. Starting early lets compounding do more of the work.
The gain or loss on an investment, usually shown as a percentage of the amount invested. Formula: return = (end value - start value + income) / start value.
example: Investing Rs 50,000 and getting back Rs 56,000 is a 12% return.

definition: Net profit divided by total assets. It shows how well a company turns everything it owns into profit.
Operating profit divided by capital employed, meaning equity plus long-term debt. It measures how well a company uses all long-term funding, borrowed and owned.
Net profit divided by shareholders' equity. It shows how much profit the company makes from the owners' money.
example: Net profit of PKR 20 crore on equity of PKR 100 crore is an ROE of 20%.

definition: An increase in equity recorded when assets like land or buildings are revalued above their book cost. It is not cash and cannot normally be paid as dividends.
The total money earned from selling goods or services before costs. Net sales is revenue after subtracting sales taxes, discounts and returns.
The other side of a repo: buying securities with an agreement to sell them back later, which is effectively lending cash against collateral.
Combining several shares into one with a higher face value. The share count falls and the price per share rises, with total value unchanged.
Any fixed, pre-agreed extra charged on a loan of money, which is prohibited in Islam. Islamic finance replaces it with trade, leasing or profit-sharing.
An extra benefit added to a main policy for an additional premium, such as accidental death, disability or critical illness cover.
The entitlement to subscribe to right shares. On PSX these entitlements can be traded separately for a short period, so a shareholder who does not want to subscribe can sell them.
New shares offered to existing shareholders, usually below market price, in proportion to their holdings, so the company can raise fresh money. You can subscribe, sell the right, or let it lapse.
example: A 1-for-5 right issue at PKR 20 lets you buy 1 new share at PKR 20 for every 5 you own.

definition: The chance that an investment's actual result will differ from what you expect, including the chance of losing money. Higher potential returns usually come with higher risk.
How much loss you can financially afford without harming your goals or daily life. It depends on income, savings, dependents and time horizon.
The extra return investors expect for taking more risk than a safe investment. For example, shares should over time pay more than government securities to make their risk worthwhile.
A label such as low, medium or high that shows how much a fund's value can go up and down. AMCs must show it so investors can match funds to their own risk tolerance.
How much ups and downs in value you can emotionally handle without panicking. It should guide how much risk you take.
The return on an investment considered almost riskless, usually a government bond or treasury bill. In Pakistan analysts typically use PIB or T-bill yields.
Risk-on is when investors feel confident and buy riskier assets like shares; risk-off is when they get fearful and move to safer assets like gold, cash or the US dollar.
The idea that to aim for higher returns you must accept more risk. Any offer of high returns with no risk is a warning sign.
Closing a futures position near expiry and opening a similar one in a later month to keep the bet going. PSX trading can get busy around rollover time.

An SBP-backed bank account that non-resident Pakistanis can open fully online in PKR or foreign currency. It can be used to invest in Pakistan, such as in Naya Pakistan Certificates, shares, funds and property.
A quick way to estimate how many years it takes money to double: divide 72 by the yearly return percentage. It also shows how fast inflation halves your money's value.
example: At 12% a year, money roughly doubles in 72 / 12 = 6 years.

definition: The effect of investing the same amount regularly: you buy more units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high, so your average cost per unit is smoothed.
example: PKR 10,000 buys 100 units at PKR 100 and 125 units at PKR 80, giving an average cost of about PKR 88.9.

definition: The return you could earn with almost no risk, usually from short-term government securities or similar. Any risky investment should aim to beat this, otherwise the risk is not worth it.
A simplified brokerage account type in Pakistan with easier opening requirements, meant for small investors. It comes with limits on how much can be invested.
A contract where the full price is paid now for goods delivered at a set future date. It is often used to finance farmers before harvest.
A tax added to the price of goods and services. In Pakistan sales tax on goods is collected by the FBR, while sales tax on services is mostly collected by provincial revenue authorities.
Shariah compliant National Savings products offered by CDNS, available as a savings account and as term accounts.
A bank account that pays profit on your balance while still letting you withdraw money. The rate can change and is usually lower than a term deposit.
The official list of fees a bank charges for services, like cheque books, transfers, cards and account maintenance. Banks must publish it.
A court- or regulator-approved plan to restructure a company, such as a merger, demerger or capital change. Shareholders vote on it first.
The SECP's online complaint system where investors can file complaints against brokers, fund managers, insurers and other SECP-regulated firms.
Where investors buy and sell existing securities among themselves after they were first issued.

aka: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
definition: The government regulator that oversees companies, the stock market, brokers, mutual funds and insurance in Pakistan. It makes rules to protect investors and can punish wrongdoing.
A group of companies in the same line of business. PSX groups listed companies into sectors such as commercial banks, cement, fertilizer and oil and gas exploration.
An index that tracks only the companies in one sector, such as banks or oil and gas. It shows how that industry is performing compared to the overall market.
Debt backed by specific assets that lenders can claim if the borrower defaults.
A loan backed by collateral. It usually has a lower rate than an unsecured loan, but you can lose the asset if you default.

term: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
definition: The regulator of Pakistan's capital markets, companies, mutual funds, insurance, NBFCs and brokers. It licenses market players and takes action against fraud.
A system where shareholders lend their shares for a fee to others who need them, often for short selling or settlement. In Pakistan it is run through NCCPL.
Money the AMC or its sponsors put into a new fund to start it, often required to stay in for a minimum period.

A weekly price measure from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics that tracks essential items such as flour, sugar, vegetables, fuel and cooking oil. It gives an early, rough signal of price pressure on ordinary households.
The final step of a trade, when the buyer's money and the seller's shares actually change hands. On PSX this happens a set number of business days after the trade.

The number of business days between the trade date (T) and settlement. T+1 means the deal settles one business day after you trade. Exchanges change this cycle from time to time, so check the current rule.
example: Under T+1, shares bought on Monday arrive in your CDC account on Tuesday.

definition: A share is a small unit of ownership in a company. If you own shares, you own a slice of the business and can receive a part of its profits as dividends.
example: If a company has 10 crore shares and you own 1,000, you own a tiny part of it.

definition: When a company buys back its own shares from the market. It reduces the number of shares, can lift earnings per share and often signals that management thinks the share is cheap. Pakistani companies may hold bought-back shares as treasury shares under SECP rules.
The money raised by issuing shares, counted at face value. Paid-up capital is the part shareholders have actually paid in.
example: 10 crore shares with PKR 10 face value give paid-up capital of PKR 100 crore.

definition: The amount received from issuing shares above their face value, held as a capital reserve.
A firm that keeps a company's shareholder records and handles dividends, transfers and physical share certificates on its behalf.
A person or institution that owns shares of a company. Shareholders can vote at company meetings and receive dividends. Pakistani company law also calls them members.
What belongs to shareholders after subtracting all liabilities from all assets. It includes share capital and reserves.
The total number of a company's shares held by all shareholders. It is used to work out per-share figures like EPS and market cap.
A regular check that an Islamic institution's actual transactions follow the approvals of its Shariah board.
A panel of qualified Islamic scholars that approves products and checks that an Islamic bank, fund or takaful operator follows Shariah. SBP and SECP also have their own Shariah boards for rules.
Following Islamic law in a product or investment: no riba, gharar or maysir, and no prohibited businesses such as alcohol, pork or conventional interest-based finance.
A fund that only invests in assets approved by its Shariah advisor, avoiding interest-based debt and businesses like alcohol or conventional banking. Most MUFAP categories have an Islamic version.

Tests used to decide whether a company's shares are Shariah compliant. They check its main business and financial ratios such as interest-bearing debt, interest-based investments, non-compliant income and the share of illiquid assets.
A share that passes Islamic screening rules, such as having a halal core business and limits on interest-based debt and income. Lists of such companies are reviewed regularly in Pakistan.
A measure of return earned per unit of risk. Formula: (portfolio return - safe rate) / standard deviation. Higher is better.
Buying back shares to close a short position. When many short sellers cover at once, it can push prices up quickly.
A position that profits if the price falls, usually created by selling borrowed shares or selling a futures contract.
Selling shares you do not own, hoping to buy them back later at a lower price. In Pakistan it is allowed only under specific SECP and PSX rules that require the shares to be available to borrow.
example: You short 100 shares at PKR 60 and buy them back at PKR 50, making PKR 1,000 before costs.

definition: National Savings certificates for short periods, such as a few months to a year, paying profit at maturity.
Loans due within a year, often bank credit lines used for day-to-day needs. Pakistani companies often call such lines running finance.
A National Savings account for the families of martyrs (shuhada) of the armed forces and law enforcement agencies, paying monthly profit.
A way to separate a defaulted or hard-to-sell holding from the rest of a fund so new investors are not affected and existing holders get recoveries later.
When prices move up and down within a narrow band without a clear trend. It often happens before a bigger move.
A precious metal used in jewellery and industry. Its price tends to swing more than gold.
Interest calculated only on the original amount, not on interest already earned.
example: Rs 100,000 at 10% simple interest earns Rs 10,000 each year, so Rs 30,000 over 3 years.

definition: A moving average where every day in the period counts equally.
Profit worked out only on the original amount, not on profit already earned.
Money saved bit by bit for a known future expense, so it does not hit you all at once.
example: Saving Rs 10,000 a month for 12 months to pay yearly school fees of Rs 120,000.

definition: A share of a company with a small market capitalisation. These can rise or fall sharply and are often less liquid.
A company's ability to meet its long-term debts. A solvent company has more assets than liabilities and can keep paying lenders.
When a government fails to pay interest or principal on its debt on time. It usually causes a currency crash, high inflation and a market slump.
An income fund that invests mainly in government debt like T-bills, PIBs and GoP Ijara Sukuk. Default risk is very low, but prices can still move when interest rates change.
A credit rating given to a country's government, showing the risk that it will not repay its debts. A better rating usually means cheaper foreign borrowing and more investor confidence.
An extra, one-time dividend usually paid from unusual profits or surplus cash. It should not be expected to repeat.
A decision at a shareholder meeting that needs a larger majority, such as changing the company's articles or approving certain restructurings.
Medium-term National Savings certificates that pay profit at regular intervals, commonly every six months. A matching Special Savings Account also exists.
Buying or selling mainly to profit from short-term price moves rather than the long-term value of the business. It can bring quick gains but carries high risk.
Shares held by the founders, parent company or main owners who control the business. Their buying or selling is closely watched as a signal.
A cryptocurrency designed to keep a steady value, usually linked to the US dollar. It is only as safe as the reserves and the company behind it, and some have failed.
A painful mix of high inflation and weak or no economic growth at the same time. It is hard to fix because raising rates to fight inflation can hurt growth further.
A provincial tax paid on legal documents such as property sale deeds, gift deeds and some agreements. Rates differ by province and change over time.
A statistic that measures how spread out returns are around their average. It is the most common number used to describe volatility.
SBP's overnight windows where banks can borrow (ceiling) or park (floor) money at fixed rates. These rates form the interest rate corridor.
Pakistan's central bank. It sets the policy rate, manages foreign exchange reserves, issues currency and regulates banks and exchange companies.
Preferring to leave things as they are, even when a change would clearly be better, such as never moving savings out of a zero-profit account.
A momentum indicator that compares the closing price with the price range over recent days. Like RSI, it flags possible overbought or oversold levels.
A licensed firm that places buy and sell orders on the exchange for you. In Pakistan brokers must be licensed by SECP and hold a trading right at PSX.
A regulated marketplace where buyers and sellers trade shares and other securities through brokers. It sets trading rules and publishes prices.
A number that tracks the combined price movement of a selected group of shares. It shows how the market or a sector is doing overall.
Dividing each share into several shares with a lower face value. The number of shares goes up and the price per share goes down, but total value stays the same.
example: A 1-to-10 split turns 100 shares of PKR 10 face value into 1,000 shares of PKR 1 face value.

definition: An order that sells your shares automatically if the price falls to a level you choose. It limits how much you can lose, though the sale price can slip below your stop in a fast market.
example: You buy at PKR 100 and set a stop-loss at PKR 90 to cap your loss near 10%.

definition: The final price at which IPO shares are sold, decided after book building. Retail applicants usually pay this price.
A specific reform step a country promises under an IMF programme, such as passing a law or changing a tax. Missing benchmarks can delay loan instalments.

A separate pot inside a VPS pension fund that invests in one asset type, such as an equity sub-fund, debt sub-fund or money market sub-fund. Your contribution is spread across sub-funds based on the allocation scheme you choose.
Money the government spends to lower the price of something, like electricity, fuel or flour. Subsidies help consumers but add to the fiscal deficit.
A legal document issued by a court, or in some areas by a NADRA succession facility, that lets legal heirs claim a deceased person's movable assets such as bank balances and shares.
Shariah compliant certificates that give holders a share of ownership in real assets or a business, and returns come from those assets (like rent or profit) rather than interest.
The amount the insurer promises to pay when the insured event, such as death, happens.
Valuing a company by valuing each of its businesses or investments separately and adding them up. Common for Pakistani holding companies and conglomerates.
Continuing with a bad decision because of money or effort already spent, even though that past cost cannot be recovered.
The State Bank of Pakistan's online complaint portal for problems with banks and other SBP-regulated institutions.
An extra income tax charged on high-earning individuals or companies above certain income levels. Its rates and thresholds change, so check the latest budget.
A price level where a falling share has tended to stop falling because buyers step in. It acts like a floor, though floors can break.
example: A share that bounced from PKR 45 three times has support near PKR 45.

definition: Money left in the takaful fund after paying claims, costs and reserves, which may be shared back with participants.
Cancelling a policy before it ends and taking the surrender value, after which cover stops.
The amount you get back if you cancel a savings or unit-linked policy before maturity. In early years it can be much less than the premiums paid.
Drawing conclusions only from the winners that survived while ignoring the many that failed, which makes success look easier than it is.
A report that a bank, broker or other regulated firm must send to the FMU when a transaction looks unusual or possibly linked to crime.
In a merger, the number of new shares you get for each old share you hold.
example: A swap ratio of 1:4 means 1 share of the new company for every 4 shares of the old one.

definition: Holding shares for a few days to a few weeks to profit from short price swings, often using chart patterns.
Investing a fixed amount in a fund at regular intervals, often monthly, no matter what the market is doing. It builds discipline and averages out the purchase price over time.
example: Sara invests PKR 10,000 every month in an equity fund by standing instruction from her bank.

definition: Risk that affects the whole market, like interest rate changes, political crises or recessions. Diversification cannot remove it.
Redeeming a fixed amount from a fund at regular intervals to create a steady income from your investment.
A Shariah compliant alternative to insurance where participants pool contributions to help each other with losses. An operator manages the pool for a fee instead of owning the risk.
The amount a participant pays into takaful, the equivalent of an insurance premium. Part of it is a donation (tabarru) to the shared risk pool.
The company that manages a takaful fund and its investments. A conventional insurer may run a separate Islamic window for takaful.
An analyst's estimate of where a share's price should be in the future, often 12 months ahead. It is an opinion, not a promise.
A deal where a person buys a commodity on deferred payment and then sells it to a third party for cash, used to raise cash in a Shariah compliant way. Some scholars restrict its use.
A detailed check by the tax authority of a taxpayer's records and return to confirm they are correct.
Arranging your affairs legally to reduce tax, such as using allowed credits. It is legal when done within the rules, unlike tax evasion.

An amount that directly reduces the tax you owe, not just your taxable income. In Pakistan credits have been available for things like eligible donations and voluntary pension contributions; the rules change, so check the current law.
An amount you may subtract from your income before tax is calculated, which lowers taxable income. Which items qualify depends on current tax law.
Illegally hiding income or assets to avoid paying tax. It can lead to penalties and prosecution.
Income or a transaction that the law says is not taxed at all, or is taxed at a reduced rate.
A formal letter from the tax authority asking for information, a return, or an explanation, or telling you of tax due. Notices have deadlines, so they should not be ignored.
Money the FBR pays back when more tax was deducted from you than you actually owed. It is claimed through your tax return.
The last date set by the FBR for filing the yearly return without penalty. It is often extended, so check FBR announcements each year.
An income range taxed at a particular rate. Pakistan's income tax for salaried and other individuals uses slabs that change in budgets.
The 12-month period used for income tax in Pakistan, running from 1 July to 30 June. It is named after the year in which it ends.
example: Tax Year 2030 covers income from 1 July 2029 to 30 June 2030 (illustrative).

definition: Total tax collected as a share of the economy's size. A low ratio means the government has little revenue and tends to borrow more.
The part of your income that tax is charged on, after allowed deductions and exemptions. It is often less than your total income.
The tax charged on a company's profits for the period, including current and deferred tax. Some Pakistani sectors also pay extra levies, which appear here.
Studying past price and volume charts to try to predict future price moves. It looks at patterns and indicators rather than company finances.
The length of time a deposit, loan or bond lasts until it matures.
Money placed with a bank for a fixed period at an agreed profit rate. Taking it out early usually means a lower rate or a penalty.
example: PKR 500,000 placed for one year at a made-up 10% earns about PKR 50,000 before tax.

definition: The receipt or certificate a bank issues for a term deposit, showing the amount, rate, tenor and maturity date.
A bond issued by a Pakistani company to borrow money for a set term, usually paying a profit linked to KIBOR. Some are listed on PSX.
Life insurance that pays only if the insured dies within a set period. It has no savings part, so it gives the most cover for the lowest premium.
In a DCF, the estimated value of all cash flows beyond the forecast years, often a large part of the total valuation.
The price of a country's exports compared with the price of its imports. When oil prices rise, an oil importer like Pakistan sees its terms of trade worsen.
The smallest amount by which a share price is allowed to move on the exchange. Orders must be placed in multiples of this step.
A short code used to identify a company on the exchange. Scrip is the common Pakistani word for a listed share.
example: A company called Example Cement Limited might trade under the symbol EXCEM.

definition: How long you plan to keep money invested before you need it. Longer horizons can usually handle more risk because there is time to recover from falls.
The legal right of ownership of a property, shown in official land records. Checking clear title before buying protects you from fraud and disputes.
A traditional South Asian unit of weight used for gold and silver, equal to about 11.66 grams. Gold prices in Pakistan are usually quoted per tola and per 10 grams.
example: If gold is Rs 200,000 per tola, a 2-tola bangle set has about Rs 400,000 of gold in it.

definition: All yearly running costs of a fund (management fee, trustee fee, regulator fees, other expenses) shown as a percentage of its average net assets. It is already deducted from the NAV, so a lower TER leaves more return for investors.
example: A TER of 2% on a PKR 100,000 holding costs about PKR 2,000 a year.

definition: Your full return including both price change and any income received, such as profit payments or dividends, usually assuming the income is reinvested.
The past performance of an investment or manager. It is useful context, but past results do not guarantee future results.
How much an index fund or ETF's return differs from the index it copies. A smaller tracking error means the fund follows its index more closely.
When a country imports more goods than it exports. Pakistan has often run trade deficits, largely due to fuel, machinery and food imports.
Money the company owes its suppliers for goods or services received but not yet paid for.
Money customers owe the company for goods or services already delivered. Large, slow-paying receivables can tie up cash.
The total rupee amount of shares that changed hands in a period. It is volume multiplied by the prices at which trades happened.
example: If 1 lakh shares traded at an average of PKR 50, traded value is PKR 50 lakh.

definition: The hours during which the exchange matches buy and sell orders. PSX publishes its session timings, which can differ on Fridays and during Ramzan.
When the exchange stops trading in one company's shares, often because of rule breaches, pending major news or a corporate restructuring. You cannot buy or sell that share until trading resumes.
Share price divided by EPS for the past 12 months of actual results.
Figures for the most recent 12 months, combining the latest quarters. It gives an up-to-date yearly view without waiting for the annual report.
A short-term government security lasting up to one year. It pays no coupon; you buy it below face value and get full face value at maturity, and the difference is your profit.
example: Buying a PKR 100,000 T-bill for PKR 91,000 and getting PKR 100,000 at maturity earns PKR 9,000.

definition: The certificate that gives a brokerage firm the right to trade on PSX. Only TREC holders can directly place orders on the exchange.
The general direction of price movement over time. An uptrend has higher highs and higher lows; a downtrend has lower highs and lower lows.
A straight line drawn on a chart connecting price lows in an uptrend or highs in a downtrend. A break of the line may signal a change in trend.
An independent company that holds a fund's assets in safe custody and checks that the AMC follows the rules and the offering document. In Pakistan this is often the Central Depository Company (CDC).
When a country has both a fiscal deficit (government spends more than it earns) and a current account deficit at the same time. It usually means heavy borrowing and pressure on the currency.
An identity number registered with NCCPL for each investor, usually based on the CNIC. It lets the clearing system track all your trades across different brokers.
Money in accounts untouched for many years that banks must hand over to SBP under the law. The owner or legal heirs can still claim it back through the bank.
Dividends that could not be paid, often because bank details were missing or wrong. Companies keep them for a period and must follow legal rules on handing them over later.
Accounts showing only the parent company itself. Pakistani listed companies with subsidiaries usually publish both these and consolidated accounts.
When a share's market price is below what an investor believes it is truly worth.
A financial institution that promises to buy any shares left unsold in an IPO or right issue. This assures the company it will raise the planned money.
The process an insurer uses to judge a person's risk, such as age and health, and decide whether to offer cover and at what premium.
People who want to work and are looking for jobs but cannot find one. The unemployment rate is their share of the labour force.
One share of ownership in a mutual fund. The value of each unit rises or falls with the fund's investments.
example: If you hold 1,000 units and the NAV is PKR 12, your holding is worth PKR 12,000.

definition: A person or company that owns units of a mutual fund. Unit holders own the fund's assets together, not the AMC.
A policy where part of each premium buys life cover and the rest is invested in funds chosen by you, so the value goes up and down with markets. Charges in early years can be high.
A person or app offering share, forex or commodity trading without a licence from the regulator. Your money is at high risk and you have no regulatory protection.
Any person or company collecting money from the public for investment without a licence from SECP or SBP. Investors have little legal protection if it fails or turns out to be a fraud.
A loan with no collateral behind it, like most personal loans and credit cards. It costs more because the lender takes more risk.
Risk that affects only one company or sector, like a factory fire or bad management. Diversification can greatly reduce it.
When a share hits the highest price allowed for the day under circuit breaker rules. Buyers pile up but few sellers remain, so trading may almost stop.
A rule that allows a short sale only at a price higher than the last traded price. It stops short sellers from pushing a falling price down even faster.
The central bank of the United States. Its interest rate decisions affect the global dollar, commodity prices and foreign money flows into markets like Pakistan.
The process of estimating what a company or share is worth, using ratios, cash flow models or asset values.
A share that looks cheap compared to its earnings, assets or dividends. Value investors buy these hoping the market will later recognise their true worth.
Costs that change month to month, like groceries, fuel, eating out or electricity bills.

Digital assets like Bitcoin that exist on blockchains rather than being issued by a central bank. Prices are extremely volatile, scams are common, and the legal and tax rules in Pakistan have been changing, so check SBP, SECP and PVARA guidance before dealing in them.
How much and how quickly a price moves up and down. High volatility means bigger swings, which means higher risk and also bigger possible gains.
The number of shares traded in a given period, such as one day. High volume shows strong interest in a share.
The idea that a price move is more trustworthy when it happens on high trading volume. A breakout on low volume is more likely to fail.
When the main owners choose to take a company off the exchange. Under PSX rules they must usually offer to buy out remaining shareholders at a fair price.

An SECP-regulated retirement savings system where individuals put money into pension funds run by AMCs. The money grows until retirement and then can be taken partly as a lump sum and partly as a regular income, under the rules.
example: A freelancer with no employer pension saves PKR 5,000 a month in a VPS pension fund.

definition: The average price a share traded at during the day, weighted by how many shares traded at each price. Institutions use it to judge whether they bought or sold at a good price.
A one-sided promise used in Islamic finance, for example a promise to buy an asset later, that supports the main contract.
The average cost of a company's funding from debt and equity, weighted by how much of each it uses. It is often the discount rate in a DCF.
An agency contract where one party acts on behalf of another for a fee. In takaful the operator manages the fund as an agent and charges a wakala fee.
The fee a takaful operator takes from contributions for managing the takaful fund.

The part of the wealth statement that explains how your net assets changed during the year, using income, gifts, inheritance and expenses. If the numbers do not add up, the FBR may ask for an explanation.

A statement filed with your income tax return listing your assets (such as property, shares, gold, bank balances) and liabilities at the end of the tax year. It must reconcile with your income and spending, so unexplained increases can draw questions.
Numbers an Islamic bank assigns to deposit types (by amount, tenor and payout frequency) to share pool profit among depositors. Higher weightage means a bigger share of the depositors' profit.
example: A 1-year deposit with weightage 1.2 earns more per rupee than a savings account with weightage 0.8 from the same pool.

definition: The average time left until a debt fund's holdings mature, weighted by how much money is in each. A longer WAM means the fund's NAV reacts more to interest rate changes.
A person who reports wrongdoing, like fraud or manipulation, inside an organisation to authorities. Regulators may offer channels and protection for whistleblowers.
Life insurance that covers you for your whole life rather than a set term, usually with higher premiums.
An index that tracks prices at the wholesale level, before goods reach shops. Rising wholesale prices often pass through to consumer prices later.
A written document saying how you want your assets handled after death. Having a clear will and up-to-date records of your investments makes it easier for your family to claim them.

Tax cut automatically by a payer (like a bank, employer or company) before paying you, and sent to the FBR on your behalf. Some withholding taxes can be adjusted against your final tax, while others are final.
example: A bank paying Rs 10,000 profit may deduct withholding tax and credit you the rest.

definition: A document from a bank, employer or other payer showing how much tax they deducted from you. You use it when filing your return to claim the tax already paid.
Tax that banks, NSS and funds deduct from profit before paying you. The rate usually depends on whether you are a filer on the Active Taxpayers List.
Current assets minus current liabilities. It shows whether a company has enough short-term resources to cover its short-term bills.
Comparing a figure with the same period one year earlier. It removes seasonal effects.
example: Profit for the quarter rose 20% YoY compared with the same quarter last year.

definition: The return you earn on a bond for the price you pay, shown as a yearly percentage. When a bond's price goes up its yield goes down, and the reverse.
A chart showing yields on government securities of different maturities, from short to long. Its shape hints at what the market expects for future interest rates and the economy.

The total yearly return you would earn if you buy a bond today and hold it to maturity, counting all coupons and any gain or loss versus face value. It assumes coupons are reinvested at the same rate.
An obligatory yearly charity on wealth above a minimum threshold (nisab) held for a lunar year, usually 2.5% of eligible wealth.
example: Eligible savings of PKR 400,000 held for a year would mean Zakat of PKR 10,000.

definition: Zakat automatically deducted by banks and NSS from certain savings balances on the first of Ramzan, unless the holder has filed a valid exemption declaration.
A declaration a person submits to the bank or savings institution to stop automatic Zakat deduction, for example on grounds of faith or school of thought.
A bond that pays no regular coupons and is sold below face value, paying full face value at maturity. T-bills work this way.
